title: Following $5.7B verdict, Taction wants a cut of iPhone and Apple Watch sales through 2035
snippet: Following a historic $5.7 billion patent infringement verdict against Apple, Taction Technology is now seeking additional damages, interest, and ongoing royalties on future iPhone and Apple Watch sales. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following a historic $5.7 billion patent infringement verdict against Apple, Taction Technology is now seeking additional damages, interest, and ongoing royalties on future iPhone and Apple Watch sales. Here are the details.

Taction seeks additional compensation

Late last month, a US jury found that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringed on two patents held by Taction Technology, awarding $5.7 billion in damages. Apple strongly disputed the verdict, arguing that its technology was fundamentally different from Taction’s, and said it would appeal.

A few weeks later, Apple asked the court to overturn the verdict or order a new trial, arguing that Taction had failed to provide evidence supporting the $5.7 billion award, leaving jurors to engage in “impermissible guesswork on a massive scale.”

Now, as spotted by Reuters, Taction has filed a motion seeking supplemental damages, ongoing royalties on future iPhone and Apple Watch sales, prejudgment interest dating back to April 2021, and additional interest from the date of the final judgment until Apple pays.

According to Taction, the jury’s award only accounted for Apple’s sales through March 2026, leaving another six months of iPhone and Apple Watch sales for which the company is now seeking compensation.

Interestingly, Taction is using Apple’s own arguments from its previous patent litigation against Samsung to support its request for ongoing royalties.

In that case, Apple argued that royalties should apply not only to products found to infringe its patents, but also to newer models using essentially the same technology.

Taction is now making the same argument, seeking to extend royalty payments to Apple’s latest devices, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12, and Apple Watch Ultra 4, which it says “are not more than colorably different from the infringing products.”

	

From the filing:

Apple itself has embraced this rule. As a patentee seeking ongoing royalties, Apple told the Northern District of California that “any ongoing royalties extend not only to ongoing sales of products found to infringe by the jury, but also to products ‘not more than colorably different’ therefrom.”

For the ongoing payments on what Taction claims are infringing products, the company is asking the court to compel Apple to provide quarterly reports of its US sales, with royalty payments due within 30 days of the end of each quarter.

Taction is proposing a 7% annual rate for prejudgment interest under California law. The company is also asking the court to extend royalty payments through September 24, 2035, when the patents in question are set to expire.

One important caveat to keep in mind: the judge has yet to enter the jury’s verdict as a final judgment, so the original $5.7 billion award and Taction’s additional demands remain unresolved, as does Apple’s motion to overturn the verdict or secure a new trial.

title: Verizon confirms $10 monthly fee for new iPhone Handoff feature
snippet: Following T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, Verizon has now confirmed how much it will charge customers to use Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, Verizon has now confirmed how much it will charge customers to use Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature. Here are the details.

Verizon customers to pay $10/month for iPhone Handoff

During Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event last month, the company shared more details about iPhone Handoff, a new iOS 27 feature first previewed at WWDC that lets users share a single phone number across two iPhones.

Apple announced that the feature would initially be supported by T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, with Verizon and EE expected to follow before the end of the year.

Shortly after the event, T-Mobile confirmed a $5 monthly fee for iPhone Handoff, while Deutsche Telekom made the feature available through its existing MultiSIM service, which costs €6.95 per month unless already included in the customer’s plan.

	

Today, as spotted by MacRumors, Verizon also confirmed its pricing for iPhone Handoff, announcing that it will charge $10 per month, twice as much as T-Mobile.

Here’s Verizon:

Verizon will support iPhone Handoff, giving customers the flexibility to use a single Verizon phone number seamlessly across two compatible iPhone models. Whether using the pocketable iPhone Duo on the go or iPhone 18 Pro for work, customers can switch active status between devices at any time while keeping full access to Verizon’s 5G network. iPhone Handoff will be available from Verizon for $10/month on compatible iPhones models running iOS 27.

AT&T, meanwhile, seemingly has no plans to support Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature. When CNET asked about it last month, the carrier acknowledged its potential benefits but said it was focused on its existing eSIM activation and transfer options instead.

title: Report: Apple’s antitrust negotiations with the DOJ spark concerns of a weak settlement
snippet: The Information reports that PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers concerned that a potential antitrust settlement between Apple and the DOJ might not go far enough in addressing the company’s allegedly anticompetitive practices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
The Information reports that PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers concerned that a potential antitrust settlement between Apple and the DOJ might not go far enough in addressing the company’s allegedly anticompetitive practices. Here are the details.

A bit of context

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Apple and the DOJ were in talks to settle a 2024 antitrust lawsuit alleging that the company illegally monopolized the US smartphone market at the expense of consumers, developers, and competitors.

When the DOJ first filed the lawsuit, Apple pledged to “vigorously” defend itself and has continued to push back against the government’s allegations ever since.

Despite Bloomberg’s report about settlement talks, the case has continued to move forward, with Apple and the DOJ recently clashing over access to internal documents from federal agencies during discovery.

However, as The Information reported today, settlement talks have also continued behind the scenes, with the Justice Department apparently prioritizing iPhone interoperability.

Settlement talks advance

According to the report, the “department appears to be focusing on a deal addressing interoperability issues developers face with the iPhone,” although developers are concerned that any resulting settlement might impose only limited restrictions on Apple’s practices.

From the report:

As part of its talks with developers, the Justice Department has asked them for a list of ways to improve the iPhone’s ability to operate with other devices, the people said.

Many developers and antitrust lawyers are concerned that the Justice Department will oﬀer Apple a settlement that imposes relatively light requirements on how its devices interact with other companies’ devices.”

According to The Information, PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers that have directly raised concerns about a potential settlement with DOJ officials.

Meanwhile, some people involved in the settlement negotiations reportedly expected a resolution much sooner, although the pending Senate confirmation of Adam Candeub, Trump’s nominee to lead the DOJ’s antitrust division, could be contributing to the delay.

The report adds that Apple has changed some of its products and policies since the DOJ brought the lawsuit in 2024, including improving messaging interoperability with Android devices, but is likely to resist more substantial changes to its ecosystem, potentially complicating efforts to reach a settlement.

Asked about the discussions, a DOJ spokesperson declined to comment on the specifics, saying only that the department would “continue to prioritize affordability for all Americans across our economy.” Other companies mentioned in the report, including PayPal and Epic Games, declined to comment, while Apple didn’t respond.

title: Google’s Universal Cart puts a shopping cart everywhere, including Search homepage, Chrome
snippet: Yesterday, Google started rolling out its Universal Cart, and the company is very prominently placing it in Search, AI Mode, Chrome, and the Gemini app. more…
fullText:
Yesterday, Google started rolling out its Universal Cart, and the company is very prominently placing it in Search, AI Mode, Chrome, and the Gemini app.

This “intelligent shopping cart” was previewed in May at I/O 2026 as a “hub for shopping on Google.” It’s meant to help “organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol.”

Universal Cart is now rolling out in the US, and we’re starting to see it in Google Search. A new shopping cart icon will appear in the top-right corner of google.com’s homepage and Search results, as well as on desktop Chrome’s New Tab Page. Clicking slides out a panel with two tabs for “Cart” and “My orders.” 

On mobile, the shopping cart appears to the left of the profile switcher in the Google app for Android. That icon also appears on the AI Mode homepage. 

	

In the Gemini app, “Cart and orders” now appears in the account menu.

This Universal Cart icon might be too prominent. It makes Google Search results that have nothing to do with purchases feel like a store page. This is incredibly jarring the first time you see it.

Google product pages gain an “Add to cart” button, with the Universal Cart letting you save products from multiple retailers. A pretty useful capability will automatically keep track of availability changes while offering price drop notifications. 

When you’re ready to purchase, Universal Cart will surface promo codes and highlight which payment method in Google Wallet will give you the most perks. Stores like Nike, Target, Walmart, and Shopify merchants will let you make purchases right from the Google interface.

title: WhatsApp may soon let iPhone users open any link in an in-app browser
snippet: After introducing limited in-app browser support for certain business links last year, WhatsApp is now working on expanding the feature to all links shared in chats. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
After introducing limited in-app browser support for certain business links last year, WhatsApp is now working on expanding the feature to all links shared in chats. Here are the details.

WhatsApp working on optional in-app browser

Last May, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp had begun testing a feature that would allow “users to view certain HTTPS-secured business sites within the app,” with the option to open those links in their default browser via the three-dot menu.

Now, the site reports that WhatsApp is working on extending this support to all in-chat links.

Although the feature is not yet available to beta testers, WABetaInfo has uncovered references to it in the latest TestFlight build and shared screenshots showing how it will work.

According to the site, a new “In-app browser” option under Settings > Chats will let users choose whether links open directly within WhatsApp or in their default browser.

Image: WABetaInfo

The same settings screen will also let users clear cookies, cache, and other browsing data stored by WhatsApp’s in-app browser.

	

Here’s WABetaInfo:

Users will be able to enable the in-app browser from the app settings. Here, WhatsApp will add a new option called “In-app browser”. When users enable this feature, they will be able to open any link they send and receive in the chat screen. When users enable this option for the first time, WhatsApp will show a bottom sheet that explains how the feature works. It informs users that they can now open any link within WhatsApp rather than in the default browser. Users will be able to restore the default browser at any time.

The report notes that “WhatsApp cannot see links shared in the conversation and which ones users open.”

As is usually the case with references discovered in WhatsApp’s TestFlight builds, there is currently no word on when the app plans to make the feature available to beta testers or the general public.

title: Minecraft and Domino’s Team Up for Block-Shaped Pizza, In-Game Freebies
snippet: Customers are randomly awarded an in-game code for either a Domino’s skin, cape or cheesy cube pet. The pizza will come in one of six Minecraft-themed boxes.
fullText:
The computer game Minecraft offers plenty of in-game food, from steak and cake to, uh, rotten flesh. Now, a popular real-world food is being mixed with Minecraft.

Beginning on Monday, Domino’s Pizza will offer Minecraft-themed tie-ins, including in-game extras, when customers buy “the Domino,” a recently launched Detroit-style pizza for one. The pizza is cut into two pieces to resemble Minecraft blocks, in connection with the new game Minecraft Dungeons II, a spin-off of the 2020 game Minecraft Dungeons.

Minecraft Dungeons II came out Sept. 29 for PC, Xbox Series X and S, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and Switch 2.

			

More from CNET

One of the six themed pizza boxes resembles a Minecraft zombie.Domino's

As part of the Minecraft collab, the rectangular Detroit-style Domino pizza will come in one of six game-related boxes, each featuring a different Minecraft Dungeons II character: the classic Creeper, Corrupted Creeper, Zombie, Pig, Prime Enchanter and the main protagonist, Valorie.

When you buy the pizza online, you can unlock a code for one of three randomly awarded in-game items to use in Minecraft Dungeons II: a Domino’s skin, a Slice Slayer Cape, and a Cheesy Cube pet.

Between Monday and Nov. 4, customers have a chance to win a free download of the game (for PC and Xbox only), normally priced at $30. Domino’s says 20,000 downloads will be given away. To enter the lottery, after purchasing “the Domino,” submit your proof of purchase on its dedicated web page.

title: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol
snippet: Figma said it plans to support as many standards as possible without exposing all of its data.
fullText:
Despite Figma co-founder Dylan Field’s concerns about MCP (model context protocol), which standardizes how AI agents connect to external data sources and tools, the company is expanding its support for the open source standard. 

At the design company’s first Config conference held in India, the company announced 20 new MCP partners, including Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode, and Sarvam Agents.

Field has expressed his misgivings about MCP before. Days before this announcement, one of MCP’s co-creators complained about Figma not supporting the open source tool Pi. As part of his response, Field made a comment about Anthropic not making its various resources available via MCP.

“I find it interesting that Anthropic (creators of MCP standard) do not expose artifacts/other cloud resources created via MCP,” he wrote on X. “The debate is framed as open vs closed. Everyone always prefers open … obviously. And meanwhile issues of asymmetric context sharing are ignored.”

(Field later added that Figma plans support Pi.)

Can you help me understand why you don't make various Anthropic resources available via MCP? Maybe I'm missing something.

— Dylan Field (@zoink) September 30, 2026

At a media briefing, I asked Field about this debate. The co-founder explained that while Figma wants to be open, he doesn’t think MCP is a perfect protocol.

“I’m really excited about what we’re doing in terms of opening up our ecosystem. I also think that MCP is not a perfect protocol. And I think that it is something that has tons of room for improvement,” the co-founder responded. “It is advantaged more to frontier labs. Also, I understand everyone online who just wants a protocol that they can use when they want to use their Figma data, and I want them to use it, too.”

Figma’s CEO said that the reason the company doesn’t want to be fully open is that the more data the company exposes through MCP, the higher the chance of abuse. 

He also clarified that while most users don’t intend to use MCP or Figma data in a malicious way, the company still has to think about those potential risks.

fullText:

YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them.

Right now, for me, the dislike button sits right next to the like button under a video. Moving it to a submenu would make it considerably more of an effort to access, meaning that fewer people would likely use it.

It’s unclear how widely this apparent test may be rolled out, and Google didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

YouTube has shown a willingness to make changes to the dislike button. In 2021, it hid the public dislike count on videos to help “protect creators from harassment,” though creators can still see dislike counts. Earlier this year, YouTube removed the dislike button from YouTube Shorts, suggesting instead that users take advantage of options in the three-dots menu.

title: Touchscreen Mac, or double your RAM or SSD size – what’s the better deal? [Poll]
snippet: We’re just a week away from the official announcement of the first ever touchscreen Mac. The upcoming MacBook Pro will also have an OLED screen, which may include a Dynamic Island, and is said to be lighter. We don’t yet know the price of the new model, but we can be sure it will carry a significant premium over the existing one. My guess would be somewhere in the $500 to $700 range … more…
fullText:
We’re just a week away from the official announcement of the first ever touchscreen Mac. The upcoming MacBook Pro will also have an OLED screen, which may include a Dynamic Island, and is said to be lighter. 

We don’t yet know the price of the new model, but we can be sure it will carry a significant premium over the existing one. My guess would be somewhere in the $500 to $700 range …

There’s so far been a fair degree of excitement about an OLED Mac. In some ways that’s certainly justified given the quality of the OLED screens we’ve seen on the iPad Pro. On the other hand, Apple’s IPS LCD panels with mini-LED backlighting have always looked fantastic, and I would say rival many competing OLED screens. For that reason, I’m expecting the improvement in display quality to be rather modest.

I’ve seen way less interest in the touchscreen. While there is certainly a segment of Apple fans who are eagerly awaiting it, the majority view seems to be that it will have limited utility and be a fingerprint magnet. My own experience of using a 12.9in iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard as a pseudo laptop is that I used the trackpad for everything except scrolling, so I don’t personally see much appeal in a touchscreen Mac.

A lighter MacBook is always welcome, of course, and if the weight difference is significant, that may be a reason to consider it. But unless it’s going to get somewhere close to the weight of a MacBook Air, it’s perhaps not worth such a substantial premium.

Assuming I’m right about the price premium, you’ll be paying somewhere in the region of $600 more for the new machine. For that much, you could double the RAM or double the size of your SSD when buying the existing model. Which would you consider the better deal?

fullText:
Apple just announced its long awaited smart home display: HomeView, and it’s available for $299. That said, the product has been in development for quite some time, being held back by all of the delays with developing a smarter Siri. 

Now that it’s on the market, some customers have had concern about the fact that you have to move the HomeView around yourself if its on a table with multiple people surrounding it. According to the Power On newsletter, it might not be too long before Apple has a solution.

We’ve known that Apple has been working on robotic products of sorts for quite some time, but now we have a clear release window. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company might debut a better HomeView, perhaps HomeView Pro – as soon as next year:

The good news is that Apple is on track to solve that problem with a souped-up version of the HomeView planned for release in 2027 or 2028. Code-named J595, this version looks like the current HomeView but has a roughly 9-inch screen (up from 7 inches) and a motorized robotic arm that lets the display swivel a full 360 degrees. Using voice recognition, the machine is designed to identify who’s speaking and automatically turn toward that person.

This version will have a larger display, and be capable of turning full-circle, rather than just a little bit of tilt. This won’t replace the HomeView, and will instead serve as a higher end model in the lineup. So, don’t expect it at the same $299 price point.

Apple reportedly also plans to use voice recognition to figure out how to pivot the robotic arm towards the right person. Think about the Center Stage camera on some newer Apple products, but leveled up.

title: The real reason to care about Vivo’s latest phone is the camera [Gallery]
snippet: The Vivo V80 sports flagship design quality, a massive 7200mAh battery, Center-Stage selfie camera, IP68/69 ingress protection, and one of the wildest AI camera modes I’ve seen yet. more…
fullText:
The Vivo V80 sports flagship design quality, a massive 7200mAh battery, Center-Stage selfie camera, IP68/69 ingress protection, and one of the wildest AI camera modes I’ve seen yet.

When I think of the smartphone industry’s best cameras, Vivo or Oppo usually comes to mind. While both companies offer good experiences on any phone they sell, their best features often appear only on flagship models. But the Vivo V80, which retails for just ₹62,999 (~$660), features the company’s new flagship AI camera mode, and that might be the single most interesting thing about the release for me.

Let’s get the full specs out of the way first. The Vivo V80’s got a 6.59-inch 144Hz OLED display, featuring 1.5k resolution, true 10-bit colors (no dithering), and 4320Hz PWM dimming at low brightness (plus an option for full DC dimming). Inside is a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4, 8GB RAM, and that massive 7200mAh battery with 90W charging. Good stuff.

The Vivo V80 uses a main 50MP Sony LYTIA 700V sensor, a 3x optical 50MP Sony IMX882 telephoto camera, an 8MP or 12MP ultrawide camera (region-dependent), and a 50MP ZEISS center-stage 90-degree selfie camera. The phone is available in India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other regions in the coming weeks.

	

To illustrate just how interesting the new AI Creation camera mode is, I took a bunch of photos using the same mode on the Vivo X500. That phone is about $300 more expensive, but it features the same AI Creation mode as the Vivo V80. The results are nothing short of jaw-dropping at times. Let’s start with the hike I took this weekend.

It was a gorgeous autumn day, but the sporadic cloud cover was really killing the vibe of my photos. The lighting was annoyingly flat, and the colors my eyes were seeing in the leaves weren’t being picked up on camera at all. So I swiped over to the AI Creation mode and hit the shutter button. The rest was all automated.

The amount of depth and color this mode added truly blew my mind. When you open the mode and point the viewfinder toward something, it scans the scene and automatically applies the style it thinks will be best. It’ll also give you two additional modes to quickly select from, or you can jump into the full UI and choose the one you want.

From here, you can also choose to have Vivo’s AI automatically remove anyone in the photo, and it does an impeccable job, too; no circling required! Original images are always available in Vivo’s Albums app, and you can select a different style after taking the photo.

This mode is 100% cloud processing, though, so you might need to wait to see the processing results if you were somewhere like I was with no signal. Processing takes about one minute per photo, and up to 10 images can be processed simultaneously. If there’s a processing limit per day, I didn’t find it. While the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 in the Vivo V80 could probably handle some of the processing, this ensures you get the best quality without much wait time.

The “Travel” category creates genuinely convincing effects like the Sunlight style. Vivo has several other options that are more dramatic and, therefore, obviously edited-looking. In the header image, I grabbed one of my son’s swords and asked him to take a picture of me. The sword and the room are fully real in these pictures, but the lighting and effects are all automatically generated by Vivo.

All of these, too, were quite convincing, despite obviously being stylized. I particularly love the mist one, although I’m not sure how often anyone would use most of these. They’re clearly only for niche dramatic photos, but hey, maybe you love that sort of thing. The rest of the options available under the “Landscape” category were initially convincing, but zooming in just a bit reveals some very obvious AI editing.

So all of this is amazing, but there’s one big problem that I’m not thrilled about: Vivo doesn’t use SynthID or another more standardized way of noting that these images are edited with AI. If you delve into the EXIF data, you can find “ai_creation” in the comments field, but Gemini apparently isn’t smart enough to understand that yet.

Most likely, Gemini and the rest will figure this out in time, but I don’t care much for AI editing tools that don’t automatically mark them as such. Vivo, if you’re reading this, please add SynthID or another way for AI tools to identify these as automated. Otherwise, this is a dope mode that I love seeing proliferate to more affordable phones like the Vivo V80, especially in the age of RAMageddon.

title: Google rolling out Universal Cart that lets you shop the web and find deals with Gemini, Search
snippet: Following its announcement at Google I/O earlier this year, Google’s new Universal Cart is now rolling out in the US, giving you the ability to shop the web and watch for deals using Search, Gemini, and more. more…
fullText:
Following its announcement at Google I/O earlier this year, Google’s new Universal Cart is now rolling out in the US, giving you the ability to shop the web and watch for deals using Search, Gemini, and more.

Universal Cart is designed to be an “intelligent” cart that works across more than just a single retailer. Through Google products such as Search and Gemini, you can save products to the cart and also pull in promo codes and monitor for deals for items in the cart.

Google says:

The cart puts you in control, helping to organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). Today, Universal Cart is rolling out in the U.S. across Google Search and in the Gemini app.

The core pitch here is the ability to add items to the Universal Cart through various touchpoints in Google services. Through Search and AI Mode, you can save shopping items to the cart, or you can do it through the Gemini app and conversations with the AI. Multiple retailers can have products in the cart with Google then linking to those retailers for eventual checkout.

	

While items are in the cart, Google will monitor for deals and price changes, alerting you if the price drops.

Similarly, Universal Cart can find “hidden” deals such as promo codes or even offers on your credit card such as cashback, helping you to change payment methods if there’s a way to score a better deal.

Google says this is powered by Wallet and that it “understands your card perks and can intelligently help you choose between payment methods.”

This is US-only for now, and comes just ahead of the busy holiday shopping season.

title: Cloud Strife, Sephiroth and Other FF7 Characters Land on Xbox Game Pass Soon
snippet: It wouldn’t be Halloween without some spooky games, too, and Xbox Game Pass has you covered.
fullText:
If you’ve never played a Final Fantasy game, October is a great time to start. Microsoft is bringing Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade, the first game in the remake’s trilogy, to Xbox Game Pass on Oct. 29. That should give you plenty of time to play the game for the first — or fifth — time before Square Enix releases Final Fantasy 7 Remake Revelation, the finale to the trilogy, in 2027.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 per month. With a higher-tier Game Pass Ultimate subscription ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month. 

The Seance of Blake Manor

Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass and Game Pass Premium subscribers can play on Oct. 27.

A woman has gone missing in this first-person detective game set in Ireland at the turn of the 20th century, and it’s up to you to find her. You play as a detective tasked with finding her, yet Blake Manor holds secrets, both occult and of this world. You’ll interrogate mystics, search for clues and navigate haunted corridors in your search. This game takes place around All Hallows’ Eve, making it perfect for this time of year.

Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade

Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass and Game Pass Premium subscribers can play on Oct. 29.

This remake of the award-winning Final Fantasy 7 retells part of the original game’s story, but this time it has updated visuals, faster gameplay and additional story elements. Whether you’re new to this classic roleplaying game or have played the original, there’s something new here for you. 

You play as mercenary-turned-eco-terrorist Cloud Strife. Your goal is to stop the megacorporation Shinra from draining the planet of its energy source, and work toward that goal with a team of folks from all over the world. Like in other Final Fantasy games, each party member has their own skills to fit your play style, giving you different avenues to tackle a range of enemies and problems.

Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 29

This classic tower-defense game is back and in high definition! So you can see the cartoony plants and zombies in all their goofy glory. This version also includes new levels and challenges for both old and new players.

Other games Microsoft is bringing to Xbox Game Pass

Those are some of the games coming to Game Pass between now and early November. Microsoft is adding these other games to the service in that time frame, too.

Sandustry (Game Preview) – Coming to Game Pass Premium on Oct. 21; previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Dodo Duckie – Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 22.

Scramble Knights Online (Game Preview) – Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 26.

Terrible Lizards –  Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 29.

Pit of Goblin – Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Nov. 3.

Games Microsoft is removing from Xbox Game Pass soon

While Microsoft is adding those games to Xbox Game Pass, it’s also removing 11 titles soon. So you’d better hurry and finish your campaigns before you have to buy these games separately.

title: TextNow’s $150 Yello Phone Is Customized for Kids and Pairs Up With a $20 Monthly Plan
snippet: The lower-cost phone has a parent portal for managing calls and texts, checking the phone’s location, and enabling games.
fullText:
Low-cost carrier TextNow launched its first child-friendly phone on Tuesday, pairing a heavily discounted Motorola handset with a software portal that lets parents control who their kid can call or text.

Yello is a customized Moto G Play that costs $150 — $100 less than the standard model’s current retail price — and comes with a $20 monthly plan, with no other required contracts or service commitments.

The Android phone restricts access to Google’s Play Store and doesn’t allow users to install additional apps or services. It’s designed primarily for calls and texts with parent-approved contacts, which parents can manage through a web-based portal that also lets them check the phone’s GPS location. Kids can call or text those contacts from a menu of large icons reminiscent of Netflix’s profile selection screen.

			

More from CNET

Yello’s software only lets kids call or text parent-approved contacts.TextNow

Other software available on the phone includes access to the cameras — a 32-megapixel main camera and an 8-megapixel front-facing camera — along with the calculator, clock and a weather app. Seven preloaded games can be enabled, which include phone classics such as Snake, Mines and Tic-Tac-Toe. Photos taken on the phone can only be shared with parents.

This more restrictive approach should let kids stay in touch with approved friends and coordinate pickups with parents while limiting distractions and access to content inappropriate for young children.

The Yello phone is identical to Motorola’s 2026 Moto G Play, pictured here.

The 2026 Moto G Play is a good choice for Yello’s software approach. When I reviewed the phone last year, I liked its larger 5,200-mAh battery because it could easily get through two days of use. But its less-powerful processor, 64GB of storage and 4GB of memory made it challenging to use as a media machine. Since Yello’s software deliberately avoids that use, the Moto G Play should be more than sufficient for calls and texts.

Despite the name, the Yello phone is available in just one color: the same soft blue on every 2026 Moto G Play that Motorola calls “pantone tapestry.”

Most US carriers offer their own versions of child-friendly devices such as Yello. AT&T, for instance, has repurposed the Samsung Galaxy A16 into the AmiGo Jr with similar parental controls. There are also a number of child-friendly smartwatches, which may be a better option depending on your family’s needs for connectivity. But Yello does offer a lot of flexibility, since it doesn’t require a more expensive unlimited data plan or a minimum service commitment.

The Yello phone is now available on TextNow’s website.

title: Google Messages adding ‘enhanced protection mode’ as Android works to combat phone scam
snippet: For Cybersecurity Awareness Month, Google is announcing new Android features to help combat messaging and phone scams, including enhanced protection mode in Google Messages. more…
fullText:
For Cybersecurity Awareness Month, Google is announcing new Android features to help combat messaging and phone scams, including enhanced protection mode in Google Messages.

Google is introducing an “enhanced protection mode” for its Messages app. Billed as providing the “most powerful and intelligent defenses” against complex scam threats, this mode starts with Scam Detection leveraging Private AI Compute. Google Messages will use “cloud Gemini models to evaluate complex message context and understand a scammer’s intent more quickly when you’re in a conversation with an unknown sender.”

This secure cloud analysis augments and extends our existing on-device detection, allowing us to identify novel and sophisticated attacks, actively uncovering and stopping abusers who try to hide their tracks

Private AI Compute, which is used by Pixel Screenshots and other apps, encrypts data and processes it in a secure space that Google cannot access for any other purpose.

The existing link protections work to flag malicious and phishing websites. With enhanced protection mode, on-device Gemini Nano uses “real-time web signals to evaluate whether an unfamiliar link is trustworthy before you tap.” This feature is available on the Pixel 10+, Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Galaxy Z Flip 8 and Z Fold 8. and “other select devices.”

	

The final feature adds redesigned warnings that “give you extra time and clearer context to pause before tapping links sent from numbers not saved in your contacts.”

This feature was previously only available on devices in select countries or on devices with Android Advanced Protection enabled 

Enhanced protection mode is an opt-in setting that is rolling out over the “coming weeks.”

Meanwhile, Google is expanding on-device Scam Detection for chat notifications beyond Pixel to HONOR, Infinix, iQOO, itel, JOVI, Motorola, OPPO, OnePlus, realme, TECNO, vivo, and Xiaomi devices. 

On the phone scam front, automatic screen-share privacy that hides sensitive info (like passwords and banking information) in native apps will soon apply to Chrome and WebView on Android 15+ devices.

Google will block apps from “quietly enabling call forwarding in the background” to combat one-time passcode theft. This call forwarding protection will be available starting in early December on Pixel and other select devices.

If a scammer attempts to trick you into manually typing an MMI forwarding code on your phone’s dial pad, Android proactively warns you before it can take effect.

title: Investigation Reveals How TikTok Executives Ignored Internal Child-Safety Warnings
snippet: NPR reports that TikTok staff raised the alarm on youth bypassing age restrictions as well as being sexually exploited on the platform.
fullText:
Court documents on some of the inner workings of TikTok paint a picture of a tech company repeatedly warned by its own staff about the dangers its platform posed to minors — and then ignoring many of those warnings.

According to an investigation from NPR, unsubmitted depositions from an ongoing multistate trial against TikTok, Meta, Google and Snap reveal that TikTok executives knew that underage users were circumventing its age restrictions. Internal documents also reportedly show that some minors were engaging in sexually exploitative acts using TikTok’s own platform features, including its Live video streaming tool.

The NPR report cites the deposition of Reagan Maher, who worked in safety at the company in the early 2020s, addressing the fallout from a damning 2022 Forbes story about child exploitation on the platform. Maher said she informed senior leaders at the company that kids aged 13 to 15 were accessing features meant for adults, such as monetized live video.

			

More from CNET

A spokesperson for TikTok told CNET in an email that the information in the NPR report was “clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works.”

TikTok also said that NPR ignored “numerous documents and resources” that would demonstrate how the story’s claims mischaracterize the platform’s features. The spokesperson stated that the company has spent significant amounts of money on safety and introduced over 50 default protections for young users, including Family Pairing tools for parents, and that it was steadfast in its “commitment to the well-being of our community.”  

Child-safety reckoning on tech platforms

TikTok is one of a growing group of major tech platforms that have faced lawsuits, scrutiny from parents and financial penalties over how they regulate the safety of younger users. Others include the gaming platform Roblox, AI companies such as OpenAI, streaming video services like Google-owned YouTube and social media companies such as Meta.

Online dangers like predators, cyberbullying and inappropriate content aren’t the only risks for kids. Tech companies are also facing lawsuits for making their platforms addictive and harmful to young users. In August, Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement over those issues in a landmark lawsuit brought on by multiple US states.

TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance — which still holds a stake in the company despite some government-mandated divestment to the US for its American operations — were sued in 2024 by the Department of Justice over violations of child privacy laws, resulting in a $400 million settlement. Last month, TikTok settled a $100 million lawsuit in Alabama and agreed to limit daily child usage in the state.

The NPR report shows not only that TikTok was made aware of these problems by its own staff. It also reveals that the company — among other alleged violations of the law — may have directly profited from the sexual exploitation of minors. Youth were reportedly rewarded with gifts online that could be converted to cash, with TikTok earning a cut of those profits.

Devastating, but predictable

Child-safety advocates told CNET that the NPR report exposes safety gaps in the way platforms such as TikTok were designed.

“These court documents are nothing short of devastating, but for those of us fighting child exploitation every day, they are tragically predictable,” said Michael Medoro, chief operating officer of Childhelp, which focuses specifically on online safety. 

Medoro said that active monitoring, the elimination of safety loopholes and stronger age verification will require cooperation between tech leaders, advocates and law enforcement. 

According to Shanna Marzilli, CEO of Plan USA, an advocacy group for girls that is part of Plan International, the TikTok documents confirm what young people, especially girls, have been saying for many years. “Online spaces are not safe for them,” she said. 

Marzilli said that young people are clued into the idea that tech companies can’t protect them. In a research study conducted among US young people aged 10 to 19, only 14% of them trust social media companies to take sexual harassment and assault seriously.

“Voluntarily implemented parental controls and self-reported age limits are demonstrably ineffective when platforms leave these structural loopholes open,” Marzilli said.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Omar Gallaga
						

						

											

								

											Omar Gallaga has covered technology, digital culture and other topics for outlets including CNET, NPR, Wired, Texas Monthly, MSNBC, Consumer Reports, The Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, The Atlantic and the Austin American-Statesman, where he was a longtime tech reporter, editor and podcaster. He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

title: Modretro’s Chromatic is more transparent and cheaper than ever; how could I not love it?
snippet: As a retro gamer, I’ve tried all manner of consoles aiming to replace my OG Game Boy Color, but not many that scratch the itch of the recently released Chromatic Transparent from Modretro. It’s, honestly, the best way to replicate the feeling of the original hardware while improving in so many key ways. more…
fullText:
As a retro gamer, I’ve tried all manner of consoles aiming to replace my OG Game Boy Color, but not many that scratch the itch of the recently released Chromatic Transparent from Modretro. It’s, honestly, the best way to replicate the feeling of the original hardware while improving in so many key ways.

I have a decent number of original gaming consoles from the 90s, but the Game Boy is arguably the handheld that I covet the most. I was a little too young to really enjoy the DMG model, but the Game Boy Color was the first EDC I ever owned. It still has a special place in my heart that very few things can match.

Luckily for me, my parents didn’t throw my original clear “Atomic Purple” Game Boy Color away under the guise of ditching clutter at home. It’s a piece of art, one that I love dearly, but it’s missing out on the fundamentals of a good gadget by 2026 standards.

Using original hardware isn’t always ideal. You miss out on a backlit display, the battery longevity is often subpar, and, in the interests of hardware preservation, I don’t want to break something that means so much to me.

	

That’s kind of why I picked up the original Modretro Chromatic last year. That is a high-end FPGA Game Boy clone that replicates software emulation with hardware-level logic recreation. You’re able to play original cartridges with supremely accurate visuals, sounds, timing, all that good stuff.

The original Chromatic was kind of pricey at over $200 with the Sapphire glass display and all-metal chassis. Sure, those are “nice-to-haves,” but the new Modretro Chromatic Transparent lowers the price of entry and adds back in the transparent tech highlight of my youth for under $150 – with a copy of Tetris. Maybe you need to be a 90s kid to truly understand the appeal. I’m just glad that brands are at least offering us these kinds of options again.

I’ve been carrying this thing for a few weeks in my sidebag in place of my orange Chromatic, and it’s a different beast in many ways. Being able to play all of my favorite Game Boy games isn’t anything new, and sure, I could use an emulator on my phone, but there’s nothing quite like playing as Nintendo intended.

From a purely holistic standpoint, you’re going back to the slow, intentional gaming that is completely vanilla. Mod-free, methodical gaming that feels intentional. I love emulation as much as anyone, but playing at 1x speed rather than trying to speedrun the grinding of Pokémon is a throwback.

Okay, it’s not a gadget for everyone. It’s more of a fancy thing that old heads will adore because it literally does one thing exceptionally well. The screen is 1:1, and includes the all-important backlighting. It does downgrade the scratch protection to Gorilla Glass, but that is far better than what the original Game Boy could ever claim.

By default, it takes three AA batteries, or you can pick up a rechargeable battery pack that charges up through the USB-C port. The port does a little more, like letting you stream to Discord and update on-device firmware. Make no mistake, the Chromatic Transparent is made for the modern era, despite doing one thing and one thing only.

I was sent the green Chromatic Clear, and it’s almost jewel-like, which demands attention. I like that it isn’t quite neon; the smoky color feels premium despite the material difference from the original Chromatic. It will pick up scuffs and dings. Personally, I see that as a patina that means I’m playing my favorite games, which, in my opinion, we should all do more of. Although some of my original carts need battery replacements, I’m using a flash cart to play through my collection.

The buttons are not quite 1:1 with the original Game Boy Color. I’d say they’re a little “stiffer” but feel about as close as you could get without being outright replicas. I know some people won’t like the D-pad. It’s marginally harder to roll through the four directions than an actual Game Boy, so some games may play a little differently.

My only major criticism is that the volume scroll wheel is too easy to adjust without intent. So be aware that you might inadvertently increase the volume while launching the Modretro settings menu.

On that, the speaker is a solitary downward-firing mono speaker, and it gets loud with no distortion. It’s amazing to hear the earworm of the Tetris theme playing at full blast, but remember to tone the volume down when you’re in public.

For anyone wondering why you wouldn’t use an original Game Boy Color to play your games, well, that’s a very fair comment. However, to get a modded Game Boy Color that has all the same functionality, it actually costs upwards of $150 from most reputable sellers on sites like eBay. Modretro is basically undercutting the original with lots of quality-of-life changes with the Chromatic Transparent.

As much as I love this hardware and will covet it in my EDC, you simply cannot separate the company from the controversial founder, Palmer Luckey. To many, the ties to his business ventures outside the gaming space will tarnish the brand. I can understand hesitation, and while I was sent this device for review, you will need to decide for yourself if you are willing to support the company. It would be unfair to omit this; hence, mentioning it.

It would also be a lie if I were not to say I’m smitten with the product. I do wish it were not marked with this extra controversy, as it’s the best way for ardent retro gamers to play through your back catalog of Game Boy titles.

For $150, the Chromatic Transparent is not a cheap way to indulge in some nostalgia. However, it’s undercutting the competition and now has even better colors to choose from.

title: iPhone Duo launch is a massive success, but Apple has a problem
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders opened today, but if you weren’t there right at the start, you likely now can’t get one before 2027. That makes the iPhone Duo launch a massive success, but also reflects a missed opportunity for Apple. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders opened today, but if you weren’t there right at the start, you likely now can’t get one before 2027. That makes the iPhone Duo launch a massive success, but also reflects a missed opportunity for Apple.

iPhone Duo had a flawless product introduction, sparking more excitement than any recent model

Before the iPhone Duo was unveiled last month, I was unsure how the public would respond to the new model. Would it seem too weird compared to standard iPhones? Would the $2,000+ price tag limit early adopters to tech enthusiasts like me?

Yet in my estimation, Apple has pulled off a basically flawless product introduction.

Starting with the September 9 unveiling, iPhone Duo’s marketing rollout has been among the best I’ve seen from Apple. The company knew it had a uniquely special product, and has given it the first-class treatment.

Anecdotally, iPhone Duo has stirred more excitement than any other recent model I can remember. Not just among “techie” early adopters, not just among the ultra-wealthy, and not even just among current iPhone users. Some of my Android friends even seem very interested.

All of this buzz was seemingly proven genuine by today’s near instant sell-out after pre-orders went live. Current shipping estimates for new orders are pushed back to late January 2027. That’s more than three months backordered—an unprecedented delay.

And today’s launch I think can be described both as a huge win and also a missed opportunity for Apple.

Instant iPhone Duo sellout is both a big win and a problem

It’s remarkable that Apple was able to introduce a foldable iPhone, which costs $2,000+, and instantly sell out. It’s amazing how much interest and excitement the iPhone Duo has garnered from a wide-ranging base of “average consumers.”

But it’s also a big problem that Apple can’t deliver anywhere close to a supply-demand balance for such a desired, ultra-premium product.

It’s not a surprise that the iPhone Duo quickly became backordered. But getting pushed out three months within 30 minutes of pre-orders opening proves just how much trouble Apple has had mass-producing the Duo.

	

Ideally, Apple would have enough supply to meet demand. More realistically, it should be able to meet initial demand within the first 4-6 weeks or so. 

But what we’re seeing is in some ways a worst-case scenario. Not just because customers will be frustrated, but chiefly because Apple is sacrificing a lot of revenue by not being able to deliver the iPhone Duo in a reasonable timeframe.

Again, overall today’s launch is a major win for Apple. But being able to capitalize more fully on its basically flawless iPhone Duo marketing plan would have been an even bigger win. Here’s hoping mass production of the iPhone Duo is able to speed up soon.

What’s your take on Apple’s iPhone Duo launch? Let us know in the comments.

title: iPhone Duo orders limited to two per customer as Apple tackles scalping
snippet: Apple is limiting iPhone Duo orders to a maximum of two per customer in the US, UK, and elsewhere after shipping dates slipped into January of next year within minutes of pre-orders opening. The move appears to be an attempt to tackle the problem of scalping, where people buy large volumes of supply-constrained devices in order to resell them on eBay for well above the retail price … more…
fullText:
Apple is limiting iPhone Duo orders to a maximum of two per customer in the US, UK, and elsewhere after shipping dates slipped into January of next year within minutes of pre-orders opening.

The move appears to be an attempt to tackle the problem of scalping, where people buy large volumes of supply-constrained devices in order to resell them on eBay for well above the retail price …

Engadget reports that it tried to add more than two iPhone Duo units to its cart on the Apple stores in the US, UK, Japan, and Spain, and received a notification advising it of the limit.

We’ve tried adding more than two units to our cart on the Apple Stores for Japan, Spain and the United Kingdom, in addition to the US, and we’ve received a warning notice across all the online stores. The notification said: “A maximum of 2 iPhone Duo can be purchased per customer. Please adjust the total quantity of iPhone Duo in your order before checking out.”

The site said that the same limit applies no matter what configuration you select.

The company is almost certainly implementing the move in a bid to reduce scalping. We’ve already seen dozens of iPhone Duos listed on eBay by scalpers, some with prices exceeding $5,000.

It’s not the first time Apple has imposed limits on supply-constrained iPhones. The company has done this in China multiple times, with limits applied to walk-in purchases in retail stores as well as those made online. The company has also done it in the US before, with the first example being the iPhone 5 way back in 2012.

9to5Mac’s Take

Industrial-level scalping is hard to defeat. Organized gangs use multiple virtual credit card numbers, email addresses, and delivery addresses in order to circumvent limits. Others pay people to place orders on their behalf.

All the same, it’s good to see Apple at least attempting to reduce the scale of the problem. It’s also possible the company is implementing other behind-the-scenes measures to detect and reject more sophisticated bulk purchase attempts.

As we predicted, some customers have seen improvements to their estimated delivery dates. It’s also worth trying for a walk-in purchase if you live close to an Apple store – just not on day one.

title: This Stunning Espresso Machine Is the Size of a Moka Pot and Inspired by a Jet Engine
snippet: What makes the 9Barista espresso machine stand out, and is it worth $740?
fullText:
When I was asked to test the 9Barista espresso machine, I couldn’t wrap my head around why a brewer that looked like a modern moka pot would cost $740 or more. After testing the 9Barista Pro espresso machine for a couple of months, I realized the company’s claim of making true espresso on your stovetop is even more impressive than the fact that the 9Barista successfully launched on Kickstarter. The British-made manual brewer is a meditation on simplicity, if you call a system that fits in one hand and uses the same principles as a jet engine “simple.” 

9Barista espresso vs. moka pot coffee

Moka pots are a classic stovetop method of making strong coffee that resembles espresso. These metal brewers are beloved for the simple three-piece construction invented by Bialetti in 1933. Cold or hot water is filled in the bottom chamber. Semi-fine coffee grounds (between fine espresso and drip coffee) fill a brewing basket placed on top of the water reservoir. A funnel feeds steaming, boiling water through the grounds into the top chamber, where the coffee collects.

Moka pots are the stovetop coffee makers most people recognize.

Brian Bennett/CNET

The original Bialetti Moka Pot is made from aluminum, and some models are made from stainless steel. Standard moka pot sizes range from one cup to 12 cups, with each “cup” measured in diminutive 2-ounce servings rather than the US standard of 8 ounces per cup.

			

More from CNET

The manual brewer is akin to a French press in the deep-roasted flavor it produces, but the moka pot yields a more concentrated coffee. You might make a bit of crema, depending on the coffee beans. A moka pot doesn’t make true espresso, however, because it can’t generate the high pressure needed to extract the coffee at espresso-level concentrations. The 9Barista espresso machine solves this issue.

The 9Barista resembles the Bialetti original because its stainless steel system still breaks into three parts and uses stovetop heat to force steam and boiling water through the beans. What sets the 9Barista apart from a moka pot is its twin-boiler system: one boiler builds nine bars of pressure, and a second regulates the temperature to 93 degrees Fahrenheit, producing a true crema-topped espresso extraction. Moka pots are said to use one or two bars of pressure. 

The clever design requires fine espresso grounds that you tamp into a basket attached beneath the top reservoir. The three parts are easily screwed together and then placed on your stovetop. Use a hot plate on electric stovetops to help distribute heat.    

The 9Barista espresso maker uses a three-piece design that comes together easily.Katherine Peach/CNET

What it’s like to make espresso on the stovetop with the 9Barista

Key takeaways: 

The 9Barista machine uses 18 grams of beans and 120 milliliters (mg) of water to produce a 1- to 1.5-ounce shot of espresso.

Aim for 3 to 6 minutes on the stovetop heat, and don’t leave it on longer than 8 minutes to avoid overheating the metal and burning the beans.

A full cleaning-and-drying cycle between shots takes 5 to 6 minutes — faster if you rinse thoroughly under cool water or don’t mind breaking it down while still warm.

The prep-to-pour time on a single shot is no more than 10 to 11 minutes.

Running the body under cold water also helps the release valve screw open more easily.

The hot plate itself changes color with use: gunmetal to copper and (eventually) back to light silver. This is expected, though it may look slightly alarming to the uninitiated.

A hot plate distributes heat when using the 9Barista on an electric stovetop; it changes color as the temperature changes.Katherine Peach/CNET

I followed the directions: 18 grams of espresso beans to 120 milliliters of water per shot. While results will vary depending on your beans, grind and timing, I found the machine produced 1 ounce (36 grams) to 1.5 ounces (43 grams) of espresso. The instructions also recommend 25 to 30 seconds for the full extraction, which is a rather standard goal for most machines. Helpful benchmarks for espresso shots: Anything extracted in under 20 seconds will likely taste thin and sour, while anything over 30 seconds will taste bitter. The goal is to find a combination that brings out the flavors you prefer. 

Heat is a new variable with the 9Barista espresso machine. When I first used the brewer, the stovetop temperature seemed like the biggest factor to dial in, especially since “medium-high heat” is, at best, a vague guideline. I recognize that the directions can only offer imprecise tips for heating your device at home, since every stove and burner behaves differently. It’s a frustrating but real variable when your stovetop becomes part of the heating system rather than a self-contained internal system. For many espresso machines, temperature control is a major selling point. Here, you’re building it yourself, burner by burner.

Steaming, boiling water forces brewed coffee into the top chamber.Katherine Peach/CNET

On the first try, I panicked that the grounds sat on the heat too long— and I was impatient—so I cranked the stovetop to 80% power. Even the internet was perplexed when I asked how a shot could pull too quickly (less than 20 seconds) and still taste bitter. Before touching the grind or the quantities, turning the heat down to 65% (6.5 out of 10 was the sweet spot) made a huge difference in flavor. Patience is indeed a virtue. Preheating the heat transfer plate while prepping the grounds also cut down on wait time and reduced how long the fresh grounds sat exposed to heat. Some reviewers online preheat the water chamber while prepping the puck separately. I prefer to turn on the whole unit at once so I can monitor the full process.

Once the plate is preheated, the directions call for 120 grams (120ml) of filtered water. There is a fill line for anyone who doesn’t want to measure. In practice, the taste didn’t vary much if I used a few milliliters less. However, I found that even 125ml of water caused the reservoir to overflow when I turned on the group head. The built-in portafilter beneath the coffee reservoir provides a sturdy, level base for tamping. A metal basket cap with an O-ring keeps the grounds in place when you inevitably flip the portafilter upside down to lock the separate components together.

Once the water starts to gurgle, it’s showtime: Steam expels from a boiler pipe for about 30 seconds before espresso accumulates in the open funnel. My early shots tended to pull shorter — around 20 seconds — and still tasted decent with a good crema.

Disassembling and cleaning the brewer gets easier with practice. The cooldown before depressurization, rinsing and drying the filter basket is what eats the time. Rinsing the group head and steel water chamber under cold water helped cool the components. I also waited to detach the group head and water reservoir, first refilling with cold water and letting it sit while I emptied the used grounds from the portafilter. The metal basket cap stays hot to the touch, so handle it carefully. I kept a thick oven mitt handy to avoid getting burned by steam from the release valve when I wanted to pull a second shot right away. A traditional moka pot makes more coffee in one go, so adjust if you’re used to that system.

The 9Barista disassembles easily for cleaning.Katherine Peach/CNET

Final thoughts on the 9Barista 

Across dozens of logged pulls, three variables kept moving at once — heat, grind and pull time — which makes any single result hard to isolate, but some patterns held up across all of my tests.

On the process itself

Heat was the dominant, hardest-to-control variable when I first used the espresso machine. Because the 9Barista relies on the stovetop rather than an internal heating system, results varied wildly by burner. The front burner took 8 to 10 minutes to boil, while the back burner boiled in under 3 minutes, both at the 6.5 heat setting. Same machine, same grind philosophy, very different extractions. 

The pressure release valve is a bit hard to grab and pull to depressurize, but the water chamber will unscrew either way if you also have trouble pulling the tiny lever outward. Considering the usual trial and error of grinding and tamping, plus those minor concerns, that’s really it in terms of challenges with the brewer. 

The hot plate system might give some people pause if they have an electric stovetop that’s prone to heat marks. This isn’t the machine’s fault. Many of my metal pans leave small traces on the stovetop at high heat, but keep that in mind if you’re a renter who wants to leave no trace. I kept half-expecting something to go wrong while the plate cycled from gunmetal to copper to silver. But this is a natural part of the heating process.

On build and usability

The 9Barista stainless steel design feels substantial in the hand, which is satisfying and suggests it’s built to last. The 9Barista espresso maker also comes with a five-year warranty, lifetime customer support, and replacement parts. While I haven’t tested the ease of a warranty claim, the time frame is well beyond most electric espresso machines. I also appreciate how the design provides a stable surface for level tamping. A traditional espresso machine uses the long portafilter handle to stabilize the basket. The difference is small but appreciated. That said, many people will appreciate this compact machine’s mobility and ease of use.

I appreciated having a level surface on which to tamp the espresso grounds.Katherine Peach/CNET

I also value 9Barista’s use of stainless steel over plastic components. Plastic often makes up water reservoirs and appears in most components of a single-serve pod coffee maker, including the espresso capsules. Plastic might be unavoidable, but anyone looking to reduce further exposure can breathe a bit easier with the 9Barista espresso machine.

Who the 9Barista is for

The 9Barista espresso machine is ideal for a household with one or two coffee drinkers who want a portable, sturdy, largely plastic-free espresso brewer. As a New Yorker, I love that this stovetop brewer takes up little space on the counter or in the cupboard. I keep reaching for the 9Barista more than I expected because it’s simple and delivers satisfying results.

The original 9Barista MK1 is a few hundred dollars cheaper.

As a former skeptic, I find the 9Barista an enticing option for smaller households or anyone who appreciates the ritual of espresso while camping outdoors. The 9Barista would be ideal for my van-life friends who weatherize their campers for winter excursions and want the comforts of home on the road. (This is a weighty machine, however, so the “every ounce counts” folks would never.) You might also see the 9Barista on the counter at your buddy’s place, the one who won’t stop talking about the sound quality of their Audio-Technica record player and bespoke speaker system. In other words, this is an investment piece that speaks of craftsmanship and innovation.

If paying north of $700 for a manual espresso maker just ain’t happening, the first-gen 9Barista MK1 is significantly cheaper at $540.

snippet: Apple just introduced HomeView alongside a new Apple TV and HomePod mini, but another product unveiling is already set for next week. Here are the new products expected to launch at Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event on October 28, including major updates to MacBook Pro and iPad mini. more…
fullText:

MacBook Pro redesign with OLED, touchscreen, Dynamic Island, more

Apple has a new MacBook Pro coming next week that’s expected to be the star of the ‘Pro and tell’ event. Rumored features include:

Industrial redesign that’s much lighter and slightly thinner

OLED display

Touchscreen

M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

No notch, just a hole-punch camera cutout and Dynamic Island

Apple is reportedly bringing its flagship A20 Pro chip from iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo to the iPad mini. The front-facing camera is also being moved to prioritize landscape use rather than the current portrait orientation.

We’re also expecting improved water resistance and a more powerful speaker system.

We’re not expecting many changes with the new iMac, as the M6 chip will be the central upgrade. Like with the M6 Mac mini (currently on sale), the iMac will gain a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and Dual 16-core Neural Engine.

Apple also has a refreshed slate of color options coming to the M6 iMac too.

In addition to the redesigned MacBook Pro with touchscreen, Apple is expected to launch a new entry-level MacBook Pro with M6 chip that’s only available in a 14-inch model.

Similar to how Apple introduced a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 last fall, we’re expecting an update to that entry model that doesn’t change much besides the M6 chip.

The M6 MacBook Pro will have the same design as the current models, and the same display technology, but be more powerful and potentially gain battery life due to the more efficient M6.

title: Apple keeps acquiring companies with one clear goal in mind
snippet: Apple acquires a variety of companies every year, and recently many of its acquisitions—including the latest, Samplab—have revolved around one clear goal: improving and expanding Apple Creator Studio. more…
fullText:
Apple acquires a variety of companies every year, and recently many of its acquisitions—including the latest, Samplab—have revolved around one clear goal: improving and expanding Apple Creator Studio.

Apple has prioritized Creator Studio with recent acquisitions, strengthening ecosystem for creatives

Next week, Apple is expected to unveil four new hardware products aimed at creatives: a redesigned MacBook Pro with touch, modernized iPad mini, and M6 versions of the iMac and MacBook Pro.

But hardware is only one part of Apple’s creator-focused push. 

All year long, the company has sought to strengthen its ecosystem of tools for creatives by launching Apple Creator Studio and acquiring companies that expand its feature set.

Apple Creator Studio debuted in January as a suite of pro apps for creatives, such as Pixelmator Pro, Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and more.

The service has regularly rolled out new features since launch, but we’ve also seen Apple invest behind-the-scenes with acquisitions that clearly have Creator Studio in mind.

In the spring we learned of two acquisitions that fit the bill. MotionVFX provided “visual effects templates, plugins, and motion graphics tools” for Final Cut Pro. Color.io brought tools for “color management and grading of digital imaging,” likely with Final Cut and/or Pixelmator in mind.

Now the latest acquisition revealed yesterday, Samplab, pitched itself as the “ultimate audio editor for musicians,” making its features a natural fit for Logic Pro. And even the recent acqui-hire of Huxe could have Creator Studio benefits too.

Why invest so much in Creator Studio? Obviously the chance to grow services revenue is reason enough. But I suspect the company also sees the app suite as a key component of its overall pitch to creatives.

Apple has long focused on bringing hardware, software, and services together in a seamless ecosystem. And its recent efforts on the software and services side are set to dovetail nicely with next week’s new hardware. All this to say, expect to see Creator Studio apps get some spotlight during Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ announcements on October 28.

Do you subscribe to Apple Creator Studio? If not, what’s it missing for you? Let us know in the comments.

title: YouTube begins rolling out GIF support for comments very slowly; it’s for a reason
snippet: It’s been less than a month since YouTube said it planned to let users post GIFs in the comments section. The time has come, and this is just the beginning of a gradual rollout. more…
fullText:
It’s been less than a month since YouTube said it planned to let users post GIFs in the comments section. The time has come, and this is just the beginning of a gradual rollout.

	

Reddit is being inundated with r/YouTube reports of users seeing GIFs in the comments under videos on the YouTube app. The conversation around the ability to post GIFs under a video is louder than the feature itself. It looks like YouTube is pushing this update in a gradual rollout, since a number of posts online center around not having the feature, but seeing them posted by other users.

YouTube said this would be coming last month, noting that users would be able to post a GIF under videos and Shorts. Any GIF posted will come from a library within the app, according to the company’s announcement. It’s unclear if users will be able to upload their own animated files.

What’s also unknown is how gradual this rollout is. Plenty of users don’t have the option, and it isn’t limited to Premium subscribers, it seems. Fortunately, YouTube is making this available slowly for the time being. Once it gets going, it’s not hard to imagine what a YouTube with a GIF-filled comments section would look like. It’s possible one may never see text in a comment again.

	

YouTube also announced other features when it broke the news about its new GIF comment system. The YouTube app will let users set custom feeds based on quick prompts, and Ask YouTube will get additional features centered around product comparisons. All three features are slated for “this Fall,” so it might not be much longer before YouTube comment sections are filled with GIFs instead of text.

title: Meta launches new Muse Spark Open model, optimized to run on Mac Studio
snippet: Meta today unveiled Muse Spark Open, which it says is the “most capable US open-weight model to date.” For Apple users, Meta says Muse Spark Open is optimized to run on the Mac Studio powered by M5 Ultra. more…
fullText:
Meta today unveiled Muse Spark Open, which it says is the “most capable US open-weight model to date.” For Apple users, Meta says Muse Spark Open is optimized to run on the Mac Studio powered by M5 Ultra.

In a blog post, Meta explains that Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and brings “leading agentic capabilities to your desktop for the first time.”

Today, we’re releasing the weights for Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window. Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

Meta’s blog post specifically touts that Muse Spark Open leverages Apple’s latest version of MLX. MLX is an open source array framework created by Apple and optimized for the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon.

Using the latest version of MLX, Meta says that Muse Spark Open was optimized for Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and that “together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.”

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra’s integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS changes to Ice Cubes (an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.

Muse Spark Open is available now through Hugging Face. Apple has also published a new article on its Machine Learning Research website touting how MLX on Mac “lets AI researchers and developers experiment locally with the latest models and methods in a private environment.”

Apple and Meta working together is a surprise given the icy history between the two companies. In an interview with Axios, Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said they are “excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again.” Wang explained that Apple and Meta have been working together for several months. Wang credits Daniel Gross, a former Apple executive, with playing a “really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together.”

title: ChatGPT gets deeper Google Chrome integration including control over tabs
snippet: OpenAI this week announced deeper integration between ChatGPT and Google Chrome, including the ability to hand control over your tabs to the AI assistant. more…
fullText:
OpenAI this week announced deeper integration between ChatGPT and Google Chrome, including the ability to hand control over your tabs to the AI assistant.

In a thread on Twitter/X, OpenAI details improvements to the ChatGPT extension for Google Chrome. The browser add-on now features deeper integration with Chrome, including the ability for ChatGPT to look at your open tabs and get things done with that context.

That starts with the ability to ask questions within ChatGPT that the AI can answer using the context of your open tabs, or even to control those open tabs to do things.

…ChatGPT can control your Chrome tabs to get things, like sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files. It can even help you organize and group that pile of tabs you have open.

There’s also a sidebar UI that you can use ChatGPT through, similar to how you can use Chrome’s built-in Gemini integration.

	

Two videos show off the integration in action:

OpenAI lists examples including:

Compare the three couches I have open by dimensions, material, delivery time, and return policy.

Explain this article in plain English. What’s the main argument, and what evidence supports it?

Compare these pricing pages against our requirements. Which plan includes everything we need?

Use the details in this event brief to fill out the registration form, and stop before submitting. 

Put the vendors in these tabs into my comparison sheet, with pricing, key features, and source links.

Look at all the tabs I have open and compare the contractor services. Then draft an email to the one that fits my home renovation.

Fill out the form I have open in @chrome ahead of seeing my new dentist. Also, can you add the appointment to my work and personal calendar.

The ChatGPT extension is now available in the Chrome Web Store.
