The iPhone Duo also features a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera, which is the same camera found in the iPhone 18 Pro. Its specifications also match the Ultra Wide camera on the regular iPhone 17.

I’ve found the Main camera on iPhone Duo to perform just as well as the camera on the iPhone Air I’ve been using as my primary iPhone for the past year. It’s a notch below the iPhone 18 Pro, but it’s not a dramatic difference. 

Here are some comparison shots between the iPhone Duo (left) and iPhone 18 Pro (right): 

iPhone Duo (left) and iPhone 18 Pro (right)

iPhone Duo (left) and iPhone 18 Pro (right)

iPhone Duo (left) and iPhone 18 Pro (right)

iPhone Duo (left) and iPhone 18 Pro (right)

The iPhone Duo also features a 12MP Center Stage camera on its outer display. That’s a step down from the 18MP Center Stage camera found on the iPhone 17, iPhone Air, and iPhone 18 Pro. You still get features like automatic framing and Dual Capture, but the Duo uses a lower-resolution camera with a smaller ƒ/2.2 aperture.

But that’s not all. The iPhone Duo actually has one more camera: a FaceTime camera located underneath the inner display.

The FaceTime camera itself is nothing to write home about, but it does get the job done for FaceTime calls. Apple hasn’t disclosed the resolution of the under-display FaceTime camera, but it supports Center Stage and 1080p video recording. If I’m on a video call or just taking a quick selfie, the under-display FaceTime camera is perfectly adequate. For anything more demanding, I’d choose a different camera.

But that’s one of the most unique things about the iPhone Duo’s form factor. You can use the 48MP rear cameras to take selfies. By unfolding the device and flipping it around, you can use the outer display as a live viewfinder while taking pictures with the higher-quality Main or Ultra Wide cameras. This means you can frame your shot and see exactly what the cameras see, without relying on the dedicated front-facing camera.

The same concept also works when someone else is taking your picture. With a feature Apple calls Duo Preview, the outer display shows a live preview of the shot, letting you check your framing and adjust your pose while the person behind the camera takes the photo.

The iPhone Duo also features Smart Take, which uses on-device AI to automatically capture a photo when everyone is posed and ready. You can prop the iPhone Duo up on a surface, activate Smart Take, and step into the frame without having to race against a timer.

Ultimately, the iPhone Duo isn’t the best camera Apple sells today. It’s a very good camera, but it’s not on the same level as the iPhone 18 Pro. That said, the versatile form factor of the iPhone Duo opens it up to new ways to use the camera hardware. As someone who used the iPhone Air up until the iPhone 18 Pro’s launch last month, I’m pretty used to life without a telephoto camera. I’d absolutely prefer having one, but it’s a tradeoff I’m willing to accept for the other benefits of the iPhone Duo’s form factor.

Odds and ends

Battery life

Here’s what Apple says about the iPhone Duo’s battery life:

Video playback on the outer display: Up to 44 hours

Video playback on the inner display: Up to 31 hours

Typical mixed use: Up to 24 hours

That “typical use” number is based on a “combination of passive and active use of a variety of applications, including but not limited to messaging, photos, music, social media, video streaming, games, web browsing, and navigation.” For iPhone Duo, the number also assumes you use both screens equally.

The iPhone Duo features a unique dual-battery architecture, with one battery in each half of the device to maximize capacity. Apple uses custom silicon and software algorithms to manage charging, discharging, and balancing between the two batteries. This lets them operate as essentially a single battery.

In my testing, the iPhone Duo has more than enough battery life to last me through a normal day. I can take it off the charger, use it normally throughout the day, and have around 20% remaining by the end of the day. I haven’t done any formal battery testing, but I’d estimate that around 60% of my usage has been on the inner display, with the remaining 40% on the outer display.

Speakers

Apple says it optimized the iPhone Duo’s speaker placement and audio tuning to deliver Spatial Audio no matter how you hold the device. That includes using it fully open, closed, or partially folded in seated and tent configurations.

I do think the iPhone Duo’s speakers leave a little bit to be desired. I wasn’t overly impressed with the speaker quality, and I think there’s a notable disparity compared with the iPhone 18 Pro. The iPhone Duo’s speakers sound thinner and quieter to my ears.

MagSafe

The iPhone Duo features MagSafe support, despite early rumors to the contrary. Existing MagSafe stands and chargers should work with the iPhone Duo. I’ve tested it with charging stands from Twelve South and Belkin so far, and haven’t had any problems.

MagSafe accessories like wallets and batteries, however, are a different story. Because the iPhone Duo is shorter than a normal iPhone, these accessories will likely hang off the bottom. This includes my beloved MagSafe Wallet straight from Apple. I suspect third-party options will pop up soon, but right now the options are pretty limited.

Performance

The iPhone Duo is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip, the same chip found in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. In my testing, performance has been essentially identical to the iPhone 18 Pro. Everything feels fast and fluid, including using Split View on the inner display.

Apple has also developed a custom thermal architecture for the iPhone Duo, including a vapor chamber and flexible graphite to help dissipate heat across its two halves. I do think the iPhone Duo runs a bit hotter than the iPhone 18 Pro, but not in a way that impacts performance.

For a deeper dive into A20 Pro performance, I have a bunch of charts in my iPhone 18 Pro review.

No Action button

The iPhone Duo doesn’t have an Action button, but it does have a Camera Control. I’d gladly swap them if given the option, and I imagine most people would agree. I’ve become accustomed to using the Action button to quickly open my AI app of choice, so its absence on the iPhone Duo is disappointing.

9to5Mac Take

Foldable smartphones have been around for years in various shapes and sizes. When most people think of foldables, I think they picture form factors like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which looks a lot more like a “normal” smartphone that happens to unfold.

The iPhone Duo doesn’t look anything like a “normal” smartphone. It’s awkward and weird on the surface, and that will turn some people off. But as soon as you unfold the iPhone Duo, it expands into an iPad-like device that is instantly recognizable.

After a week with the iPhone Duo, I’m convinced that this form factor represents the future of the iPhone. There’s something special about a compact, notebook-like iPhone that unfolds into a tablet-like experience, and it just makes sense once you start using it. Importantly, neither screen feels compromised. I’ve been repeatedly surprised by how capable the outer display is compared to what I expected. 

That said, the iPhone Duo is a first-generation product, and it comes with trade-offs. From a hardware perspective, most people will notice two things: it has Touch ID rather than Face ID, and it lacks a telephoto camera.

I also think there are aspects of the software experience that need to catch up to the hardware. Apple’s overarching software philosophy is on the right track, but there are places where iOS could do more to take advantage of the larger inner display.

At $1,999, the iPhone Duo is an expensive proposition, especially when you consider the features you’re giving up compared to the iPhone 18 Pro. For most people, a traditional iPhone is still the practical purchase right now. 

But over time, I think that calculation will change. The iPhone Duo is a glimpse at the future of the iPhone, and that future is foldable.

title: Samsung rolling out major Health update with Sleep & Running coach, meal scanning
snippet: The Samsung Health app is getting a pretty major update this week with support for new coaches for sleep and running, as well as support for scanning meals to track calories and macros. more…
fullText:
The Samsung Health app is getting a pretty major update this week with support for new coaches for sleep and running, as well as support for scanning meals to track calories and macros.

Starting with its new coaches, Samsung Health will now offer tips and help build checklists to improve their sleep quality, as well as getting analysis on their sleep tracking data (from Galaxy Watch or Ring) to identify trends. 

Samsung explains:

Informed by principles of behavioral sleep science, the program gives users daily habit checklists and sleep tips — supporting users in building routines around everyday wellness, such as avoiding screens an hour before bed, skipping late caffeine and stretching outdoors after waking up.

Users can also enjoy more intuitive and detailed analysis reports. The new pentagon-shaped Sleep Balance graph consolidates five key aspects of sleep indicators —sleep time, sleep regularity, awake time during the night, sleep satisfaction, and Energy Score— to provide an at-a-glance view of sleep trends and areas that may warrant attention, based on data collected or inputted through sleep coaching.

Beyond that, Samsung Health’s Running Coach is also getting upgrades with new training levels, a social media sharing feature, and deeper integration with Strava. This includes importing Strava running, trail, and cycling routes into Samsung Health.

	

The other big addition here, at least for users in the US, is “Scan Meal.”

This new beta feature allows users to take a photo of their meal and have Samsung Health leverage AI resources to identify the food and the serving size and provide an estimate of calories and macros. This isn’t some wild new idea – Google Health does the same – but it’s certainly convenient if you’re already invested in Samsung Health. This also comes with a new “Diet Score” feature that helps you adjust your diet to support goals such as eating vegetables, upping protein, or limiting sugar and processed foods.

Samsung says:

Using data inputted into the feature, users also receive a Diet Score, calculated through a Samsung nutrition assessment model. Similar to the Sleep and Energy Scores, which utilize on-device and cloud-based algorithms to analyze users’ activity data, the Diet Score is categorized into four tiers — Needs Attention, Fair, Good, and Excellent — to provide users with a general snapshot of certain aspects of their eating habits. The diet data that is input is analyzed through seven focused dimensions, spanning food groups and beverage and food habits, guiding users to manage their food intake to support diet choices like eating vegetables and proteins while limiting sugar-sweetened beverages and ultra-processed foods.

These updates are rolling out now.

title: Some Google Home Speakers downloading massive amounts of data in the background
snippet: The new Google Home Speaker has an issue where it downloads hundreds of gigabytes of data in the background for some owners. more…
fullText:
The new Google Home Speaker has an issue where it downloads hundreds of gigabytes of data in the background for some owners.

Over the past week, several reports have emerged about how the Google Home Speaker appears to be continuously downloading data from company servers.

In my case, a Google Home Speaker that has not been used in the past day for voice commands or media streaming consumed 17 GB of data in 24 hours. At 3 a.m. PT, it downloaded 9.99 GB. Given the timing, this could be related to failed attempts to download device firmware. 

Meanwhile, on October 13, the same speaker downloaded 41 GB of data. Over the past 30 days, the total download comes in at 132 GB.

	

It’s not clear if this is a widespread issue. Another lightly used Home Speaker of ours (in a different household) downloaded only 2 GB of data in the past month. 

	

Most routers let you check how much data a particular device has used. If you’re using Nest Wifi, go to the Google Home app’s Wifi top tab > Devices > select your speaker > Device usage graphs. You can switch between 1-, 7-, and 30-day graphs.

We’re not seeing this download issue with other Google Home and Nest devices, including several Nest Hubs in the same house as the affected Home Speaker.

If you have multiple Home Speakers and a limited data plan, this issue could easily breach your cap, as some have found.

In a statement to 9to5Google today, the company acknowledged the issue and said “a fix is already rolling out that should address this for users.”

title: Apple is looking for a cellular modem engineer to help shape its transition to 6G
snippet: Apple is looking for an experienced cellular modem systems engineer to help develop its next generation of cellular modems as the company transitions toward 6G. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple is looking for an experienced cellular modem systems engineer to help develop its next generation of cellular modems as the company transitions toward 6G. Here are the details.

‘A rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication’

As spotted by MacRumors, Apple listed a new job opening yesterday for a 6G Cellular Modem Systems Engineer, with a base salary range of $175,000 to $308,500 per year, plus stock awards and other benefits.

From the job listing:

We’re looking for a Cellular Modem Systems Engineer to join our cellular systems engineering team as we define and build the next generation of cellular technology. This is a rare opportunity to shape the future of wireless communication at a company that ships at global scale as we transition towards 6G. In this role, you’ll bring an end-to-end view of wireless systems — spanning 3GPP standards, feature definition and planning, design, hardware and software architecture and partitioning — to deliver leading-edge performance and power optimizations and features that directly improve the user experience across Apple products. If you thrive at the intersection of deep technical theory and hands-on bring-up — and you’re excited about pushing beyond 5G into the 6G era — we want to hear from you.

Apple says the candidate’s responsibilities will include defining features and requirements for next-generation cellular modems, designing algorithms to improve performance and power efficiency, and working with hardware and software teams to bring those technologies to market.

The candidate should have a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field, along with at least 10 years of industry experience working with cellular technologies.

Apple also requires a strong understanding of cellular communication standards and proficiency in MATLAB, C/C++, or Python.

Interestingly, Apple also lists experience with generative AI and LLM-based tools “to accelerate engineering workflows” as a minimum qualification. Ideally, the candidate should also have a track record of published research or patents in wireless communications, among other preferred qualifications.

For context, 6G is still years away and in the early stages of development, as companies and industry organizations work to define what it will look like.

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) has outlined potential peak speeds of up to 200 Gbps, compared to 5G’s theoretical maximum of 20 Gbps, along with research targets for latency as low as 0.1 milliseconds.

AI is also expected to play a much bigger role in 6G, helping networks automatically adjust to changing conditions, optimize signal quality, manage traffic, and reduce power consumption.

The first official 6G technical specifications are expected to be finalized in late 2028, with commercial networks and compatible devices anticipated around 2030.

title: MapQuest App Shows You Where License Plate Readers Are in Your Area
snippet: Turn on the Surveillance option and you’ll see tiny eyeballs on the map marking the cameras’ locations.
fullText:
The roads have eyes, and MapQuest can now show you where they are. The navigational app added a feature this week that lets you discover where Flock cameras and other automatic license plate readers are in your neighborhood and beyond.

In a post on Bluesky, MapQuest said its app shows locations of license plate readers from Flock and many other companies — Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), Genetec, Axis Communications, Axon, Leonardo (ELSAG), Neology, Rekor, PlateSmart, Ubicquia, Verkada and more.

To activate the feature, open the MapQuest app, tap the Layers icon and turn on the Surveillance option. You will then see tiny eyeballs on the map that indicate where license plate readers are located. If you click on an eyeball, it will show what type of license plate reader it is — dome or fixed, for example — and the exact coordinates.

			

More from CNET

MapQuest has been riding a wave of relevance, years after being relegated to lower-tier status by the likes of Google, Apple and Waze. In August, MapQuest refused to change Lake Ontario to Lake America in its maps despite President Donald Trump’s executive order. It then muscled into Android Auto to give drivers an alternative to Google Maps on their dashboards.

But MapQuest isn’t the first app to reveal locations of license plate readers. The others include DeFlock, FlockHopper, Pelican and LPR Maps. Some of them rely on crowdsourcing — drivers notify the app when they believe they have spotted a license plate reader and where it is.

Read more: How to Tell if a New Neighborhood Device Is a Flock Surveillance Camera

Displaying surveillance camera locations was among the top three requests among MapQuest users, general manager Doug Bergen told CNET.

“In the last month, we’ve been inundated with direct requests from our users,” Bergen said. “They want to know where cameras are and what kind they are. Adding that information gives them a clearer picture of the road ahead and more choice in what their map shows.”

Bergen said that camera location data comes from OpenStreetMap, a global map of the world built by volunteers.

Although license plate readers have been around for decades and there are more than 140,000 all over the US, the technology has become highly unpopular. Flock cameras can collect a huge trove of data from a car: its license plate, make, model and color, and its location. Civil liberties groups and others say that all this information — input into law enforcement databases across the country — helps to create a mass surveillance network that can track everyone, not just suspected criminals.

There have been instances of Flock data being misused, such as police officers stalking ex-spouses and girlfriends and people being wrongly pulled over and accused of stealing their cars.

License plate readers are also used for more mundane operations, such as electronic toll collection on roads and bridges, traffic violations, parking enforcement, vehicle repossessions and parking gate activation for access to restricted areas.

I’m surrounded by license plate readers

I tried the new MapQuest feature. Being more of a Google Maps person, I didn’t have the MapQuest app, so I installed it on my phone.

I opened the app, found the Surveillance layer and turned it on. I was greeted by a bunch of eyeballs on the map in my city and county. I clicked on several of them and saw their coordinates and what type they were — dome, fixed, pan/tilt and so on — but I didn’t see the names of the companies that own them.

But at least now I know which streets have eyes on me.

Payday’s first full-VR game is on the cusp of release, but you don’t have to wait! Join the playtest now and get exclusive rewards when the full game releases on November 5.

It’s almost hard to believe we’re getting such a big-name VR release like Payday: Aces High this late in 2026, but the release is almost upon us, and the second public play test has already begun! Not familiar with the Payday series? Maybe you’ve been hiding in a bank vault for the past decade and a half, but the concept is pretty simple. You and three other “professionals” take on missions to rob higher and higher profile targets, grabbing as much sweet loot along the way as you can.

	

Meta Quest 3S on Amazon

Payday: Aces High rewards players for stealth and clever play, meaning you earn more on missions you don’t botch. The co-op gameplay requires real teamwork if you want to last, and the VR version takes this to new heights with natural body language and emotions, plus an entirely new story with new protagonists (called The Aces) to play as. As players earn cash and other in-game currency, they can unlock new weapons, traps, masks, and abilities, so your time is fully rewarded.

I got to play an early version of Payday: Aces High back in August, plus the first play test, and as a fan of the series, I can tell you this is an incredible entry. This week’s play test includes a second mission that wasn’t in the first play test, so you can rack up even more experience before going into the final game in a few weeks. title: Android Auto ‘Work Account’ support would allow for easy switching in work vehicles
snippet: Support for work accounts was recently discovered in an unreleased version of Android Auto. It could be a perfect feature for users who need to connect to their work vehicle without personal apps enabled. more…
fullText:
Support for work accounts was recently discovered in an unreleased version of Android Auto. It could be a perfect feature for users who need to connect to their work vehicle without personal apps enabled.

Android has an existing separation of data for work apps. Work Accounts lets users divide personal and business accounts, isolating the data and applications between them. For users who have Work Profiles enabled, a small briefcase icon signifies whether these apps are turned on or accessible. Those apps then run in separate instances.

Android Auto has not and still does not officially support Work Profiles. But an unreleased version of the app shows signs of support, discovered by Android Authority. The Android Auto build (18.0.664204) adds Work Account to the Quick Settings tile options.

Similar to how it functions on mobile Android, enabling it lights up a briefcase icon over the app drawer, so you know those app versions are enabled. The test version isn’t fully functional, but it may mean Google is planning to add a critical function for some users to Android Auto.

	

Work Account support in Android Auto would be a great addition for work or corporate vehicles. Those who spend work hours behind the wheel are missing out on support for those apps, hindering the experience Android Auto tries to provide.

There’s no telling if or when Work Accounts get support in Android Auto, but it’s appearance signals it might be soon.

title: HomePod is about to get free upgrade with these new features
snippet: Apple unveiled three new Home products this week: HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K. While there’s no new full-size HomePod launching, Apple did announce three features coming to the existing HomePod 2 via a free software update. more…
fullText:
Apple unveiled three new Home products this week: HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K. While there’s no new full-size HomePod launching, Apple did announce three features coming to the existing HomePod 2 via a free software update.

#1: Sound Glow

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone, your HomePod will get the new Sound Glow feature that’s also coming to HomePod mini 2.

Per Apple’s webpage for HomePod (2nd generation): “with Sound Glow, the top of your HomePod lights up with colors that match your album artwork, pulsing in tune with the music.”

The HomePod mini 2 announcement adds more details, which hopefully will be the same on the larger HomePod:

With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod mini transforms into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble. The song’s album artwork from Now Playing generates a color-matched light experience that’s unique to every song, and users can pick a soundscape like rain to trigger bespoke animations for a soothing atmosphere.

#2: Default speaker for Mac

Apple has long let you use a HomePod as a speaker for your Mac via AirPlay. But soon, you’ll be able to set HomePod as the default Mac speaker for a more seamless, reliable connection.

Like Sound Glow, Apple announced this feature for HomePod mini 2, but its fine print says:

Compatible with HomePod mini 2 and HomePod (2nd generation) with support on all Mac desktops and laptops with Wi-Fi 6E or later.

So if you want to upgrade your Mac speaker setup with the HomePod, or a stereo pair of HomePods, that will soon be easier than ever.

#3: Surround sound with four HomePods and Apple TV 4K

If you want the best, all-Apple home theater experience, a new surround sound feature for HomePod and Apple TV 4K will deliver that.

Exclusive to the new Apple TV 4K (4th gen), users can set up four HomePods—two as front speakers, two as rear—for a more immersive audio experience.

From Apple’s press release:

Home theater surround sound requires four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) speakers in matching pairs (front and rear), paired with Apple TV 4K (4th generation) running the latest operating system software.

Apple hasn’t yet confirmed when these new features are launching on HomePod, but they’re expected to debut with iOS 27.2 and HomePod 27.2 later this month.

title: Google says fix for Android Auto’s missing signal icon is rolling out, and it actually is [U]
snippet: After weeks of back and forth, Google has officially confirmed a fix is rolling out for Android Auto’s missing signal icon. more…
fullText:
After weeks of back and forth, Google has officially confirmed a fix is rolling out for Android Auto’s missing signal icon.

The corner of every Android Auto display is meant to show your phone’s battery status, the time, a number of notifications, and your phone’s current cellular connection status.

The last one has been in rough shape.

While it hasn’t been consistent or fully widespread, many have found the cellular signal icon on Android Auto vanishing off and on for several weeks now. Recent updates have seemed to fix the issue for many, but now Google is confirming a fix has been made. In a comment on Reddit, a Google representative explains:

	

We’re aware of reports about the missing cellular signal, and we’re actually currently rolling out a fix that should hopefully address this issue! The fix isn’t widely available yet, though, so it may take some time to reach your device – if you want to receive it sooner, though, you can enroll in the Android Auto beta

The Android Auto beta program, notably, is full at the moment, but you can sideload updates (at your own risk). 

Android Auto 17.8 seems to deliver the fix, at least in part, and is now rolling out via the stable track.

Update 10/16: Google first confirmed the signal bar fix was rolling out earlier this month and, in the past day or two, it seems to have widely rolled out as more user reports have popped up, one of which points at Android Auto 17.8 as the reason. It’s still not back for everyone, it seems, but most users finally have this long-running bug fixed.

title: iPhone Duo sells out immediately, now backordered until next year
snippet: iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone, went up for pre-order today. Within minutes of pre-orders opening, however, estimated delivery dates started slipping all the way to next year. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone, went up for pre-order today. Within minutes of pre-orders opening, however, estimated delivery dates started slipping all the way to next year. 

The first iPhone Duo pre-orders are set to arrive on October 23, but only for the lucky people who placed their order in time. 

As of 8:30 a.m. ET, all iPhone Duo configurations are backordered until next year. All color and storage combinations show an estimated ship date of January 25. Some users are even seeing January 29 for their estimated shipping date.

This is a combination of strong demand and severely constrained supply for iPhone Duo. It’s impossible to know the exact balance between the two, though.  

	

Going into the launch, there were multiple reports suggesting iPhone Duo would be in short supply as Apple was still ramping up production. A report from Nikkei Asia last month said Apple was making just a few hundred iPhone Duo units per day, significantly behind the ramp of a normal iPhone launch. 

A quick glance on eBay reveals that there are already dozens of iPhone Duos available for pre-order from scalpers, asking as much as $5,200.

fullText:
Exercise-tracking platform Strava announced today a new expansion of its strength training features, adding coach-designed guided workouts with live set and rep tracking. Here are the details.

Strava expands strength training features

A few months ago, Strava announced an overhaul of its strength training experience, with a dedicated workout log for tracking sets, reps, and weights, automatic muscle maps, and more.

Now, users can track their sets and reps as they go, with the results automatically saved to their activity once the session ends. The muscle maps introduced earlier this year will also update to reflect the completed exercises.

Here’s Strava:

Rolling out to subscribers over the next few weeks, with a sample workout available to free users, the new experience walks athletes through workouts developed by experienced strength coaches with guided animations, and lets them track sets and reps live as they go. Clicking into each exercise also provides guidance on the correct form, tips and the exact muscles targeted. When a workout ends, every exercise, set, and rep is saved directly to the athlete’s activity, and their muscle map updates to show where the effort went.

The company said today’s update also introduces new guided running workouts, with additional workout series planned before the end of the year.

And speaking of what’s coming, Strava says it’s working on a feature that will let users import strength workouts simply by uploading screenshots of training plans or notes containing sets and reps, “as well as a build-your-own workout feature.”

title: Apple Watch warned a veteran about a health problem he didn’t know he had
snippet: Apple Watch sleep apnea notifications launched two years ago. Since then, the health feature has been quietly working in the background and making a difference for people who may not know they need it. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch sleep apnea notifications launched two years ago. Since then, the health feature has been quietly working in the background and making a difference for people who may not know they need it.

Apple Watch Ultra flagged a serious health issue for an Air Force veteran

A new story from Military.com highlights one such case involving David Aladejobi, a 38-year-old Air Force veteran whose Apple Watch alerted him to possible sleep apnea.

Aladejobi initially brushed off the possible sleep apnea Apple Watch notification. After thinking about his snoring, however, he contacted his doctor and shared a screenshot of the alert. He had also been experiencing headaches that his doctor suspected could be related to sleep.

“I got the notification saying, you may have sleep apnea through the watch. I didn’t really think much about it. But then, I started thinking about how I was snoring and stuff like that.

So, I contacted my doctor and sent a screenshot of what the watch was saying,” Aladejobi said, in an interview with Military.com. “I was also having headaches and my doctor was saying it might be because of sleep.”

A sleep apnea diagnosis followed, along with a referral to a sleep lab and a prescription for a CPAP machine to help regulate his breathing overnight.

“Yeah, my doctor said undiagnosed sleep apnea, if not treated, can definitely lead to death or other health problems like high blood pressure,” he said. “So using something as simple as a watch that’s already being worn and already paid for, and then being urged to see a doctor. That was huge. Why not pay attention to something like that?”

How sleep apnea notifications work

Apple Watch uses its accelerometer to identify breathing disturbances during sleep. The feature evaluates those disturbances over a 30-day period and can notify users when the data shows consistent signs of moderate to severe sleep apnea.

Apple says users need to enable sleep tracking and wear a compatible Apple Watch to bed for at least 10 nights during that period. Notifications are intended for adults who haven’t already been diagnosed with sleep apnea.

The notification itself isn’t a diagnosis. Like for Aladejobi, it provides a reason to contact a doctor about symptoms and potentially get treatment for an otherwise unknown condition.

Apple Watch possible sleep apnea notifications work with Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 9 or later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 or later.

title: Samsung’s Android 18-based One UI 10 update sounds like it might be a big deal
snippet: While Android 17 is still trickling out to Android phones, Samsung is undoubtedly cooking up its Android 18-based One UI 10 update behind the scenes and, based on some early leaks, it at least sounds like it could be a reasonably big one. more…
fullText:
While Android 17 is still trickling out to Android phones, Samsung is undoubtedly cooking up its Android 18-based One UI 10 update behind the scenes and, based on some early leaks, it at least sounds like it could be a reasonably big one.

One UI 10 rumors call the update ‘significant’ 

Rumors about Samsung tend to get overhyped. Tiny details get too much attention and there’s always some drama mixed in for good measure.

That said, early rumblings around One UI 10 make it sound like there’s actually something worth being excited about. Ice Universe says that the update will bring “significant changes, unprecedented in nature.” Also having popped up is the term “Galaxy OS,” though there’s not been much weight behind that both in terms of where it came from and that the rumor itself doubles back on that name. 

In both cases, though, a big update is claimed to be in the works.

	

Samsung is overdue for an overhaul, but what will it be?

While there’s not much to talk about in terms of actual features yet, Samsung is due for a bigger update this year.

The last major update to One UI came with One UI 7 back in 2024, bringing with it overhauls to the lockscreen, app drawer, and more. The roots of that update arrived in One UI 6 a year prior, but it was the Android 15 update that brought the welcome overhaul.

Since then, Samsung’s updates have been pretty tame. One UI 8 (Android 16) delivered quality-of-life tweaks and some app updates while One UI 8.5 later built on that with some Liqud Glass clones and more design and functionality tweaks.

One UI 9, based on Android 17, is currently rolling out and it’s one of the smallest updates in recent memory. 

One UI 9: All the features you need to know [Video]

Samsung has updated these Galaxy devices to Android 17

What could One UI 10 bring to the table? It’s genuinely hard to know at this point. Virtually every other Android brand has been diving into straight-up Liquid Glass clones lately, and there’s no reason to think Samsung won’t succumb to the same. 

Making it harder to know what’s on the way is that we don’t know much about Android 18 itself yet. Google has teased some new graphics features that developers can leverage and it doesn’t feel like much of a leap to assume that Samsung could lean into that. Google teased “delightful mesh gradients” and “progressive blurs” powered by these new features, with the Android Dev Summit set to detail more on that next week. 

What would you want from One UI 10? Let us know in the comments below!

title: Apple Photos in iOS 27 upgrades one of my favorite features in a big way
snippet: Apple Photos is full of exciting updates in iOS 27, including for one of my favorite features in the app: iCloud Shared Albums. more…
fullText:
Apple Photos is full of exciting updates in iOS 27, including for one of my favorite features in the app: iCloud Shared Albums.

Apple’s Photos app is one of my most-used apps, as I suspect it is for many iPhone users. It’s where all of the photos and videos I capture live, plus screenshots, pictures shared by friends, and more.

But did you know that the Photos app also has a social media-style feature?

I’m not big on social media, but I do enjoy having a private, social-lite way to share memories with loved ones. And iCloud Shared Albums offers exactly that.

With iCloud Shared Albums, you can create an album that’s shared with only the people you choose. Anyone invited can add their own photos and videos, and you’ll get notified when they do. You can also ‘like’ shared photos and comment on them—just like a proper social network.

I’ve used and enjoyed Shared Albums for a long time, but the feature has felt in need of some upgrades. Fortunately, iOS 27 provides them.

In iOS 27, Shared Albums now support full-resolution photos and videos. That’s a huge item checked off my wish list.

Additionally, iOS 27 expands how you can react to a photo or video. Now you can use any emoji of your choosing as a reaction—you’re not limited to just ‘likes.’

For the first time, Android and Windows users can contribute to the album via the web. Previously, they could only view content shared by Apple users.

Apple has also made it easier to save shared photos with a tap. And you can set new participant permissions and optionally have your album expire at a later date.

These upgrades address all of the complaints I’ve previously had about Shared Albums. Combined with the other improvements in iOS 27, it’s a big year for Apple Photos.

fullText:
Wyze has released a new BodyScan Plus scale that syncs with Google Health and Android Health Connect while fixing a long-running problem with scales – this one actually lets you see the display.

Available starting today as a part of “Wyze Week,” the Wyze Scale Ultra BodyScan Plus continues its mouthful of a name, but with some nice features to back it up.

The Wyze Scale Ultra Bodyscan launched in late 2025 with this new Plus model being its sequel. It’s a bit more expensive at $149 – what isn’t more expensive in 2026 – and makes one key hardware change. Where the original made itself stand out by putting sensors on a bar that you could raise up to get more details on muscle mass and more, it still put the display at your feet, making it a bit harder to see those results. 

Wyze Scale Ultra Bodyscan Plus moves the display over to that bar, letting you see everything way closer to eye level. 

	

When just tracking weight without the added sensors, the display is still at your feet, but the bar lets you lift that up for easier readability. 

That’s on top of the scale supporting the same metrics including “weight, BMI, body fat percentage, muscle mass, body water, visceral fat, protein, bone mass, basal metabolic rate,” and others. The scale requires no subscription, nor does it even require a Bluetooth connection to your phone. Built-in Wi-Fi means it can sync with the Wyze app on its own while also being able to connect into Google Health and Apple Health, as well as leverage Android’s Health Connect to tie into other apps.

title: Qualcomm says rumors about Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating are ‘inaccurate’
snippet: Following a report that Samsung might skip the latest Snapdragon flagship, Qualcomm says that rumors about the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 running into overheating issues are “inaccurate.” more…
fullText:
Following a report that Samsung might skip the latest Snapdragon flagship, Qualcomm says that rumors about the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 running into overheating issues are “inaccurate.”

For context: Reports out of Korea suggest that Samsung is in talks with Qualcomm to address overheating issues with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, with Samsung weighing its options and considering skipping the chip for its own Exynos 2700.

It’s a big claim, and one that Qualcomm says is “inaccurate.” 

Responding to the story, Qualcomm tells 9to5Google that it is “proud of the innovation and strong momentum behind our next-generation flagship platform” and that reports of “thermal issues” are “inaccurate.”

	

A spokesperson says:

Recent reporting about thermal issues related to Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is inaccurate. We are proud of the innovation and strong momentum behind our next-generation flagship platform and continue to work closely with global OEMs to deliver premium user experiences.

In a reply on Twitter/X, Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire reiterates that there are “no systemic thermal issues.”

There are no systemic thermal issues with the 8 elite gen 6. OEMs are consistently tuning their platforms as they launch their products. Always trying to balance performance and power to optimize their value props around different use cases. We work together to deliver the best…

— Don McGuire (@donnymac) October 16, 2026

Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 packs two 5GHz cores and some massive CPU and GPU performance improvements over the already-powerful Gen 5 flagship. 

Qualcomm announces the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6

Devices already confirmed to use the new top-tier chip include Motorola Signature 27, Xiaomi 18, Redmagic 12 Pro Plus, Honor Magic 9 Pro Max, OnePlus 16, and more.

fullText:

You might not think about it often, but the Phone app on your iPhone keeps getting more powerful. Here are two features you can use today, plus one coming next month in iOS 27. 

Hold Assist

With iOS 26 last year, Apple added a new feature called Hold Assist to the Phone app. When you’re on a call, the feature can detect when you’ve been placed on hold. Then you’ll see a pop-up you can tap to enable Hold Assist.

When the person on the other end of the call returns, your iPhone will notify you.

Here’s how Apple describes Hold Assist: “Automatically detect when you are placed on hold, so you can step away. iPhone will then notify you when it’s time to pick up.”

You can enable Hold Assist by going to the Settings app, scrolling down to Apps, then choosing Phone. In this menu, you’ll see a toggle: “Hold Assist Detection” that you can turn on.

Call Screening

Call Screening is another new feature in the Phone app, introduced as part of iOS 26 last year. Here’s how Apple describes it: “Calls from unsaved numbers will be asked for more information before iPhone rings.”

When someone from an unsaved number calls you, Call Screening kicks in and asks who they are and why they are calling. You can then view their explanation right on your iPhone’s Lock Screen and choose to answer or send them to voicemail.

In an age of ever-increasing spam calls, Call Screening is a must-enable feature. You can find it in Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Phone.

Call Context

Finally, Call Context is a new feature coming to the Phone app with iOS 27. It’s an Apple Intelligence feature that proactively surfaces relevant information when you call a business.

For example, if you call an airline to change your flight, Call Context will automatically find your confirmation code in Mail and show it on the screen while you’re on the call. If you call a company about a recent order you placed, it will proactively surface the order number and other relevant details.

Call Context is a well-done feature that uses AI to proactively help you during what is often a frustrating process. It also does so with privacy in mind, and only looks at who you’re calling, not what you’re saying, to show the necessary information.

Call Context is available on iPhone 15 Pro and later.

Wrap up

I try to avoid using the Phone app at all costs, but unfortunately it’s a necessary evil. These new Phone app features at least make the experience more enjoyable. In particular, I’m a huge fan of Call Screening. I get an absurd number of spam calls every day, and Call Screening really helps me preserve my sanity.

What are your favorite Phone app features? Do you use any of the new options? Let us know down in the comments.

by  Richard Lawler

Oct 20, 2026, 11:04 PM UTC

Image: The Verge

Richard Lawler

 

is a senior editor following news across tech, culture, policy, and entertainment. He joined The Verge in 2021 after several years covering news at Engadget.

On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.

When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, “Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about our family, and especially Sam… All of these claims are utterly untrue. This situation causes immense pain to our entire family.”

Bluestone granted Sam Altman’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled in that court, while denying Sam’s request for attorney fees and costs. Santos Perez, a lawyer who had represented Ann until withdrawing this month, told The Guardian in a statement that “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

title: You can now join a WhatsApp call without an account
snippet: WhatsApp is making it easier to makes calls with everyone by introducing the ability for non-WhatsApp users to join a call without needing an account. more…
fullText:
WhatsApp is making it easier to makes calls with everyone by introducing the ability for non-WhatsApp users to join a call without needing an account.

Detailed in a blog post today, WhatsApp no longer requires an account for you to join a call. This works by sharing a link with another user who can then join that call through the web, and it works with calls of all sizes, whether that’s one-on-one or up to 32 people.

Calls with users invited via link remain end-to-end encrypted and all users retain the same core features such as the ability to raise their hand, share their screen, and more. And WhatsApp calls remain free with no time limits.

WhatsApp says:

	

To get started, navigate to the Calls tab in WhatsApp, select the “+” icon, create a call link, and send it to the people you want to talk to – colleagues, classmates, or tutor – without having to worry about what apps they have. Guests can open the link in their computer browser, type in their name, and join 1:1 and group calls with up to 32 people once admitted by the host. Only people with a WhatsApp account can create a call link.

The post further adds that these links will soon be integrated into Google Calendar and Outlook using a WhatsApp plugin.

title: Nest’s Halloween doorbell chimes are live now through November 1
snippet: With Halloween just a couple of weeks away, it’s the perfect time to make sure you’re ready for trick-or-treaters. It’s not enough just to buy candy in bulk, of course; you’ll also need to make sure your home feels appropriately spooky, and with Nest’s annual Halloween doorbell chimes now available, the hardest part is already done for you. more…
fullText:
With Halloween just a couple of weeks away, it’s the perfect time to make sure you’re ready for trick-or-treaters. It’s not enough just to buy candy in bulk, of course; you’ll also need to make sure your home feels appropriately spooky, and with Nest’s annual Halloween doorbell chimes now available, the hardest part is already done for you.

Google began rolling out its Halloween-themed doorbell chimes to users yesterday, as spotted by 9to5’s Ben Schoon. This year includes nine different tones to swap between at any time, and thanks to a recent app update from Google, you can preview them without having to ring your own doorbell. As with all of Nest’s seasonal chimes, you’ll find these settings available in the Home app under “Seasonal themes.” You should see a prompt right from the main page in the app.

If you’re looking to make the most of this year’s spooky chimes, though, make sure you set it up as soon as possible. With Halloween on a Saturday this year, these are set to wrap up more or less immediately on November 1st — you know, All Saint’s Day…month. And if you don’t plan on handing out candy to any trick-or-treaters this year, don’t forget your chime is easily disabled from the settings menu.

title: WaPo: Apple revealed as one of the top donors to Trump’s White House ballroom
snippet: A new investigation by The Washington Post reveals that Apple and Nvidia each pledged $25 million toward Trump’s new White House ballroom, making them two of the project’s largest donors. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new investigation by The Washington Post reveals that Apple and Nvidia each pledged $25 million toward Trump’s new White House ballroom, making them two of the project’s largest donors. Here are the details.

Apple and Nvidia tie for largest donations overall

Last October, CNN reported:

 “Apple, Amazon, Lockheed Martin, Microsoft, Google, Coinbase, Comcast and Meta are just some of the major companies who have made donations to build President Donald Trump’s proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom, according to the White House.”

The controversial project, whose estimated construction cost has climbed to $600 million, has now come under even closer scrutiny following a new investigation by The Washington Post, which obtained internal fundraising records containing previously undisclosed details about donors and the amounts they committed.

According to the report, Apple, Nvidia, the Adelson Family Foundation, and the Charlie Ergen household and donor-advised fund each pledged $25 million, collectively accounting for roughly 30% of the $333 million in reported contributions.

The numbers are from an internal spreadsheet obtained by The Post.

	

While Apple’s involvement was already public knowledge, the amount of its contribution had not previously been disclosed.

Other donations associated with the tech sector reportedly include:

Google via John P. Coale Esq. Trust: $22 million (through settlement funds from Trump’s lawsuit against YouTube)

Microsoft: $10 million

Palantir: $10 million

Amazon: $5 million

Meta: $5 million

HP: $2.5 million

Micron: $2.5 million

Salesforce: $2 million (with another $1 million from Benioff DAF)

The list also includes $5 million contributions from Cisco, Coinbase, Ripple, ServiceNow, and T-Mobile, as well as $1 million from cryptocurrency exchange Kraken and space-station developer Vast Space.

title: Your HomePod has a colorful new party trick: how to enable Sound Glow
snippet: Apple is rolling out a new feature for HomePod mini and the second-gen big HomePod called Sound Glow. This lights up the touch surface of your speaker with colors that reference the album artwork of the currently playing song, perhaps adding some additional ambience to a party vibe. Here’s how to enable the new Sound Glow feature … more…
fullText:
Apple is rolling out a new feature for HomePod mini and the second-gen big HomePod called Sound Glow. This lights up the touch surface of your speaker with colors that reference the album artwork of the currently playing song, perhaps adding some additional ambience to a party vibe.

Here’s how to enable the new Sound Glow feature …

Sound Glow is supported by HomePod mini and HomePod mini 2, and the second-generation HomePod. The original 2018 HomePod is not supported.

	

Sound Glow shows animated ambient light effects based on what’s playing, so you have to be playing music or a podcast with album artwork for it to work. In practice, you see two or three dominant colors from the artwork appear on the illuminated surface. The balls of color bounce around to give a bit of motion.

The output brightness of a HomePod ‘screen’ is not that bright, but if you have the HomePod against a white wall, you can get some visible color cast in a dark room, even if you can’t see the top of the HomePod itself.

How to enable Sound Glow on HomePod

To enable Sound Glow, make sure to update to the latest software version 27.2 (currently in release candidate beta). Then, open the Home app, long-press on your HomePod and scroll down to the settings. There will be a new toggle for Sound Glow. Just enable it to activate and start playing music to see it in action.

You can also enable Sound Glow from the Control Center on an Apple TV, when paired to HomePods. Long-press on the Apple TV remote, scroll across to select the HomePod menu item, and then click to enable or disable Sound Glow. It’s quite handy that it is easily accessible here as that means you can quickly turn it on if you are hosting a party, and easily turn it off for the rest of the year when it might be too distracting.

title: Apple poaches longtime Meta executive to lead global litigation
snippet: Bloomberg reports that Apple has hired Scott Tucker, who spent nearly six years as Meta’s vice president and deputy general counsel for global litigation. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Bloomberg reports that Apple has hired Scott Tucker, who spent nearly six years as Meta’s vice president and deputy general counsel for global litigation. Here are the details.

Apple’s legal team overhaul continues

Earlier this year, Meta’s former chief legal officer Jennifer Newstead joined Apple as its new general counsel, replacing longtime executive Kate Adams.

Newstead’s responsibilities eventually expanded to include government affairs following the retirement of Lisa Jackson, who had previously overseen the division.

The changes brought Apple’s legal and government affairs teams under a single executive, with former CEO Tim Cook, now Apple’s executive chairman, also remaining directly involved in managing the company’s government relations.

As part of the reorganization, Apple also hired former American Airlines executive Nate Gatten as its new vice president of government affairs.

Now, Bloomberg reports that Newstead is bringing in a former colleague from Meta, Scott Tucker, who joined Mark Zuckerberg’s company in 2021 and previously held a senior legal position at Morgan Stanley.

The company has hired Scott Tucker, a longtime deputy general counsel and litigation chief at Meta, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

[…]

Tucker is becoming Apple’s vice president of global litigation and financial services, a newly created position overseeing commercial and patent litigation worldwide, said the people, who asked not to be named because the move isn’t public. He’ll also manage legal matters involving the company’s financial offerings.

The report adds that as a result of Tucker joining the company, Heather Grenier, Apple’s vice president of commercial and competition litigation, will now report to him rather than directly to Newstead. Bloomberg notes, however, that Grenier will retain her position on Newstead’s legal leadership team.

Finally, Bloomberg says Apple is also expanding the responsibilities of longtime legal executive Kyle Andeer, who will now oversee matters involving “international legal matters and functions involving online child safety, cybersecurity and law enforcement.”

title: The COROS Pace 4 is a smartwatch for running and clear reasons to buy over Wear OS
snippet: Acclaimed Japanese marathon champion Suguru Osako’s special edition COROS Pace 4 lasts a whopping 19 days on a single charge, including over 41 hours of real-time GPS tracking. more…
fullText:
Acclaimed Japanese marathon champion Suguru Osako’s special edition COROS Pace 4 lasts a whopping 19 days on a single charge, including over 41 hours of real-time GPS tracking.

If you’re a runner, chances are, you’re already using a COROS smartwatch. But if you’ve been using one for a while, you might want to consider the company’s latest watch, named after acclaimed marathon runner Suguru Osako, which brings a unique style along with the COROS Pace 4’s already top-notch specs.

For the basics, this one packs a 1.2-inch AMOLED display with completely flat glass up top and a 6000-series aluminum alloy casing to keep it protected.

A unique yellow action button adorns the left side, letting you quickly use your voice to start or control a workout, make voice notes, and set reminders. I’ve used the voice notes feature more than once during a run to remind myself of something that happened, usually during a trail run, in my case.

	

The whole package comes in a matte gray-green colorway with a unique, supple silicone band adorned with Osako’s motto, “now or never,” which may just give you the boost you need during a particularly strenuous run.

Like the regular Pace 4, the Suguru Osako edition comes with free workout and training plans, race predictor, virtual pacer, personalized marathon plans, and a lot more in the COROS app.

You can buy it right now at COROS for just $289, making this a surprisingly affordable way to track all the miles you’re about to run to keep warm this winter.

Why choose a COROS Pace 4 over Wear OS?

We certainly love our Wear OS watches for their extraordinary capability and deep integration into Android, but even after years of evolution and innovation, most of them suffer from the same big issue: battery life. Take the Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 on my wrist in the photo above, for example. I took it out for a hike on Saturday and didn’t wear it at all yesterday (Sunday), yet it’s at 7% battery already.

The COROS Pace 4 would still be in the 90-95% range after the same exact scenario, and it’s why I almost never wear Wear OS watches anymore. And I’m definitely not alone here. When I go to my weekly run club, at least half of the folks there use a COROS watch, with the remaining watches typically bearing Garmin or Amazfit branding. Rarely do I see people using Wear OS or Apple Watches there.

There’s also no subscription fee just to get access to your data (or a virtual training coach), as the COROS app has everything built in. So if you’re an athlete that’s sick of your watch being dead every time you want to use it, COROS is the right choice, and that’s just one of many reasons runners love the brand.

title: Jason Sudeikis gives update on Ted Lasso seasons 5 and 6
snippet: Ted Lasso season 4 wrapped up earlier this month, and there’s still no official word on the show’s future. But on a recent podcast appearance, Jason Sudeikis shared a new update on Ted Lasso season 5 and beyond. more…
fullText:
Ted Lasso season 4 wrapped up earlier this month, and there’s still no official word on the show’s future. But on a recent podcast appearance, Jason Sudeikis shared a new update on Ted Lasso season 5 and beyond.

Here’s the current status of Ted Lasso season 5 and beyond

On a new episode of the podcast Talk Easy with Sam Frogoso, Jason Sudeikis discusses his experience returning to Ted Lasso for season 4, and addresses the current status of season 5 and plan for more seasons.

After season 3 concluded, Apple and it seemed the entire cast wanted more Ted Lasso. But repeatedly in interviews, everyone involved deferred to Sudeikis when asked about a potential season 4. The creative leader behind Lasso wasn’t sure if he wanted the show to go on.

This time around, however, things sound different. 

Here’s what Sudeikis said during his podcast appearance about more Ted Lasso seasons:

Sam Frogoso: So what does this all mean for you moving forward? You want to keep going back to the well? Do you have season five and six mapped out? Is that the plan?

Jason Sudeikis: I mean, that was the endeavor of going back into it, just sort of like, oh, I think there’s more in there…We’ll see. It takes a village.

Frogoso: Do you want to do it?

Sudeikis: I would like to, yeah. I think it would be fun.

Frogoso: You’re being mighty coy about whether there’s going to be more seasons of the show.

Sudeikis: Oh, unintentionally.

Frogoso: Do you just not know?

Sudeikis: Yeah, I just don’t know. We haven’t started a writers room or anything like that.

Frogoso: But Apple would do it if, presumably, you want to keep going.

Sudeikis: I would assume so.

Reading between the lines, it sounds like there are some behind-the-scenes negotiations still ongoing regarding additional seasons.

Before season 4 began, reporting indicated Sudeikis had a new three-season arc in mind for the show. That’s what Frogoso refers to in his initial question. And while Sudeikis sounds fully onboard and ready to move forward with his plan for more seasons, clearly something is holding up the show.

	

During its season 4 run, Ted Lasso was consistently the top-viewed show on Apple TV. While it didn’t hit nearly the heights that season 3 enjoyed, it was still very much a hit for the streamer.

If you’re looking for another Apple TV comedy to watch, Small Prophets has been hailed as “the finest show to hit Apple this year.”

title: iPhone Duo orders are delayed into 2027; here are the Android foldables you should try instead
snippet: The iPhone Duo is already delayed for months just hours after pre-orders have opened, leaving those interested in foldables unable to get Apple’s take anytime soon. If you’re seriously interested in a foldable, though, may I interest you in some Android alternatives? more…
fullText:
The iPhone Duo is already delayed for months just hours after pre-orders have opened, leaving those interested in foldables unable to get Apple’s take anytime soon. If you’re seriously interested in a foldable, though, may I interest you in some Android alternatives?

Apple opened up pre-orders for the iPhone Duo earlier today and, as our sister site 9to5Mac points out, delivery dates slipped immediately. The first wave arrives later this month but, within less than an hour, every configuration had been delayed to January 2027 or later. 

Oof.

So, if you really want to try out a foldable, here are some Android alternatives to take a look at.

	

Galaxy Z Fold 8: Same difference

The obvious choice here is Galaxy Z Fold 8, the foldable that’s directly benefiting from the sheer existence of iPhone Duo. And that’s largely because the comparisons are obvious. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 shares nearly the same form factor as the iPhone Duo with its short and wide outer display, and its wide inner display. It also has virtually no display create, an anti-reflective display (admittedly much less aggressive than Apple’s), and the same basic camera setup.

Review: The Galaxy Z Fold 8’s new shape isn’t for you – it’s for everyone

It’s more or less the same phone, just not made by Apple. That does mean you’re losing out on some of Apple’s integrations, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 does support iMessage-like texting over RCS, as well as AirDrop support with MacBooks, iPad, and other iPhones. 

And it’s cheaper, too.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 starts $100 less than the iPhone Duo at $1,899, but it’s frequently on sale and easier to find around $1,600-1,700 at any given time.

Samsung.com

Best Buy

Amazon

Motorola Razr Fold: For the stylus and battery

If you don’t want Apple’s exact form factor, the Motorola Razr Fold is an underrated option. Starting at $1,899, it has a typical smartphone display on the outside and a square-ish inner display. That bigger canvas is still useful for multitasking and media just like the Duo, just in a different shape.

Motorola Razr Fold Review: Shockingly great

The benefit of Razr Fold is that you get a way bigger battery than anything Samsung is offering, as well as stylus support on both displays. They’re both big reasons to go for Motorola’s foldable.

Motorola.com

Best Buy

Oppo Find N6: If you can get it

If you can get it, and that’s a big “if,” the Oppo Find N6 is absolutely worthy of consideration.

Like the Motorola Razr Fold, it has a huge battery and stylus support, but with stronger cameras and a thinner design, as well as one of the best display creases in the business. The software, especially following the latest ColorOS update, will also feel very iPhone-like.

But, in the US, it’s almost impossible to get it.

The Oppo Find N6 is the best foldable you can’t buy, again

Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: The standard for a reason

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra isn’t the “new” option, but it’s still a great one. A thin chassis, all of the camera lenses you’d want, and a bigger battery than past generations while checking every box in terms of hardware and software features.

Review: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra ticks every box, but it’s the boring option now

Not exciting, but excellent. And heavily discounted quite frequently. You can get a Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra for around $1,899 pretty easily, around $200 off its usual price, and it’s well worth your consideration.

Samsung.com

Best Buy

Amazon

Honorable mention: Pixel 11 Pro Fold

Google’s Pixel series is one of the standouts in the industry because it’s not just copying Apple’s playbook. And, if you’re going to switch away from iPhone, this might be the best place to go. Between clean and stable implementations of cross-platform features like RCS, AirDrop over Quick Share, and more, the Pixel is very much the best choice in terms of experience alone.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold, however, lags behind in the overall foldable space. It’s a perfectly fine foldable that’s still thinner than Apple’s, but it also lacks the polish of Samsung’s foldables. 

Review: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold just barely keeps up

It’s fourth-best, but that’s still “last” for the time being. You’ll be happy with it, just don’t expect anything crazy.

title: ‘Tenzing’ premieres on Apple TV, starring Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston and Willem Dafoe
snippet: The newest Apple Original Films feature, “Tenzing,” is now available to Apple TV subscribers. Watch the trailer below. more…
fullText:
The newest Apple Original Films feature, “Tenzing,” is now available to Apple TV subscribers. Watch the trailer below.

’Tenzing’ now available to stream on Apple TV

A few days ago, Apple Original Films held a limited theatrical premiere of “Tenzing,” its latest adventure film starring Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston (The Life of Chuck), and Willem Dafoe (At Eternity’s Gate).

Interestingly, “Tenzing” is the second mountain-climbing release set against an icy backdrop to debut in recent days, following the October 2 premiere of the documentary “The Last First: Winter K2.”

And although “Tenzing” is not a documentary, it is based on a true story. Here’s how Apple TV describes the film:

Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), was the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling.

October has been a busy month for Apple TV, with premieres including “The Last First: Winter K2,” the British comedy-drama “Small Prophets,” and the John Cena-led action film “Matchbox The Movie.”

In the coming weeks, Apple TV will also premiere the second season of “Where’s Wanda?” and the thriller series “Nocturne,” along with “Heart,” a true-crime podcast centered on a haunting story.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 is excellent, but I find myself missing this one software feature
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 has been a marvel of an upgrade, at least for me. I’ve written about it WHOOP. That said, in my past month testing it, there’s one WHOOP feature I’ve found myself missing. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 has been a marvel of an upgrade, at least for me. I’ve written about it many times, and personally – I have found that the Apple Watch Series 12 is a competent replacement for the WHOOP. That said, in my past month testing it, there’s one WHOOP feature I’ve found myself missing.

Yes, I know – the Series 12 is old news, and there are much cooler things to think about, like iPhone Duo and HomeView. That said, the Apple Watch Series 12 was quite charming to me, primarily because it felt like a little bit of a surprise.

We knew we’d be getting an always-on heart rate monitor, and we knew Apple was working on a new Health app, though we didn’t know when it would ship. Seeing the two together actually felt like quite a novel launch. That’s besides the point, though. Let’s talk about the redesigned Health app and what I feel it’s missing.

New Health app

Frankly, Apple did a lot really well here. For one, there’s the fact that the interface actually feels easy to read and navigate. On top of that, the new features like Readiness and Health Age make it feel like a much more meaningful app. Plus, existing features like Vitals and Sleep being integrated means I’ll actually go look at it daily.

This Health app isn’t shipping yet. It was available in iOS 27.2 for a little while, but has since been removed. Apple says it’ll come back in a later iOS beta prior to releasing it later this year. In all likelihood, this means iOS 27.3, which should enter beta before the end of the month and ship before the end of December.

What I’d like to see

For me, and this is more of a small personal preference than a true flaw with the app or how it’s designed, I’d really like to see Apple copy WHOOP’s approach to measuring days: sleep.

With WHOOP, your days aren’t measured on a fixed 24 hour clock, they’re based on when you go to sleep. That means if you do a workout past midnight, it still counts for the existing day. Or, if you were out late at night, your walk home counts towards the day that you started on, rather than counting towards the next day. I personally prefer this concept of tracking fitness goals.

Of course, it could be an option, though I do think fixing peoples “days” to their sleep is a little more sensible than basing it on a normal clock, especially when it comes to tracking exercise.

What do you think of this concept? How do you feel about the new Apple Health app? Let us know in the comments.

title: iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro: Here’s every key difference
snippet: Apple has strong pitches for all of its flagship iPhones this fall, but which model is right for you? Here’s an overview of the key differences between iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple has strong pitches for all of its flagship iPhones this fall, but which model is right for you? Here’s an overview of the key differences between iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.

Form factor and dimensions: Foldable vs traditional

It’s the most obvious difference, but should be stated regardless. With iPhone Duo you get a very different form factor: it’s a foldable device. With iPhone 18 Pro, you get a traditional iPhone experience.

If you’ve never used a foldable, it’s hard to explain the difference in how each model might feel in practice. But generally speaking, with iPhone Duo you get essentially an iPhone and iPad in one device. The displays are unique shapes and sizes compared to a traditional iPhone though, which may take some adjustment.

Here is how each model’s dimensions compare:

iPhone Duo might seem more sleek than iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it ultimately weighs slightly more.

Displays: Dual vs single in varying sizes

iPhone Duo has two displays: a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch folding display.

With iPhone 18 Pro, you can choose from the standard 6.3-inch size or 6.9-inch Pro Max model.

So with the Duo, you can enjoy a “small iPhone” experience while also having the option of a larger inner screen than what iPhone 18 Pro Max offers.

iPhone Duo’s folding display also comes with a nano-texture finish, a first in an iPhone.

Cameras: Clear advantage for iPhone 18 Pro

Cameras are one of the most important iPhone features. And in this department, iPhone 18 Pro is the clear winner.

iPhone 18 Pro has the new 48MP Main camera with variable aperture. iPhone Duo lacks the variable aperture feature, so its Main camera lags behind the Pro line.

With iPhone 18 Pro, you also get the Telephoto camera that’s missing from iPhone Duo.

In terms of software features, each model has its own unique exclusives:

iPhone Duo: Smart Take, Kid Cue, Duo Preview

iPhone 18 Pro: Smart focus tracking, Pro controls, Apple Reference Image

iPhone 18 Pro also exclusively supports ProRes video recording up to 4K at 60 fps with external recording, a “studio-quality four-mic array,” Spatial video recording at 1080p at 30 fps, Spatial photos, ProRes RAW, Genlock, and more.

Battery: Excellent battery life on all models

Because iPhone Duo has two displays, its quoted battery life varies depending on which display you’re using. But overall, Apple is promising strong battery life on both the Duo as well as iPhone 18 Pro.

Here are Apple’s quoted numbers:

iPhone Duo outer display: Up to 44 hours

iPhone Duo folding display: Up to 31 hours

iPhone 18 Pro: Up to 36 hours

iPhone 18 Pro Max: Up to 45 hours

Everyone’s use patterns will differ, but if you split the difference between the two iPhone Duo battery estimates, you’re looking at around 38 hours in average video playback.

All the other big and small differences: Face ID, buttons, software, Apple Pencil, more

Authentication differs between iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, with the former using Touch ID and the latter Face ID.

iPhone Duo does not have an Action button, but does offer Camera Control.

iPhone Duo comes with several multitasking advantages in iOS 27, like the ability to use apps in Split View and have unique landscape views. It also has other fun software additions like a partially-folded StandBy mode.

Apple Pencil (USB-C model) will be supported on iPhone Duo later this year, another advantage over iPhone 18 Pro.

A new C2 modem is included in both iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, but iPhone 18 Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem.

Colors for iPhone 18 Pro are Burgundy, Glacier, Black, and Silver. iPhone Duo only offers two colors: Star White and Night Sky.

Finally, design materials differ: iPhone 18 Pro has an aluminum unibody design, while iPhone Duo uses titanium.

Pricing and availability: Big gaps in both

Pricing is another major difference between Apple’s new models. Here are starting prices for 256GB models:

iPhone Duo: $1,999

iPhone 18 Pro: $1,199

iPhone 18 Pro Max: $1,299

iPhone 18 Pro has been available for nearly a month, while iPhone Duo pre-orders just went live today. However, if you haven’t ordered one yet, shipping estimates are already delayed into 2027. So if you need a new iPhone sooner, iPhone 18 Pro is the way to go.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6: The Release Trailer You’ve Been Waiting For
snippet: The wait is over, and it’s looking good.
fullText:
Rockstar Games is on the final stretch of a long and winding road: The Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer arrived on Oct. 15. In an incredibly popular but chaotic series, the new trailer hits different, featuring a new, haunting track from Justice, featuring Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. We’re obsessed with it all.

It seems like the wait has been worth it. The launch trailer captures a feeling that the other games haven’t quite managed to reach. It was almost a year ago that Rockstar Games announced it would be releasing GTA 6, and now we’re getting closer to its Nov. 19 release date for the Xbox Series X, Series S and PlayStation 5. 

The story centers around a character named Jason, who used to be in the army, but admits he “got into some trouble,” and that they “don’t give loans to people like me.” When he gets a call from the other central character, Lucia, the story begins, and we’re swept into the adventure and chaos. 

			

More from CNET

GTA has always been a choose-your-own-adventure type of game. Personally, I’ve never played through the storylines, instead preferring the open-world nature of doing anything you want in an extensive setting. But this trailer has me intrigued and wanting to know what happens to our main characters. 

The new background track is dynamic and sad, suggesting that the story that will unfold won’t be your typical smash-and-bash game. 

GTA 6 has been in development for an extremely long time — GTA 5 came out in 2013 — and we’re about to see just what the fruits of Rockstar Games’ labor are all about. Get ready for a new ride that should bring old GTA lovers and newcomers on board.
